error_message: Cross-tenant data leak via permissive service-scan RLS policy USING(true) TO hive_app on agent_tasks (PR #333, caught in review pre-merge)
root_cause: Postgres OR-combines all PERMISSIVE policies for a role+command. A blanket USING(true) SELECT policy added for a background worker cancels the tenant_isolation policy for EVERY hive_app SELECT, because Get/List filter tenant via RLS only (not in SQL WHERE). Third occurrence of this class (egress #308, RAG #232 prior).
fix: Never add a blanket table RLS policy to the shared app role for a cross-tenant background job. Use a SECURITY DEFINER function scoped to exactly the job query, or a dedicated BYPASSRLS role/connection. Always add a regression test: a 2-tenant authenticated user still cannot Get/List another tenant row after the migration.

error_message: column "tenant_id" does not exist on clean supabase db push at 20260625_06_audit_cold_archive_manifest.sql (CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... (tenant_id, partition_month))
root_cause: audit_cold_archive_manifest defined twice with incompatible shapes: 20260516_04 (May, partition_name/parquet_path) and 20260625_06 (June, id/tenant_id/object_key). June used CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so on a chained fresh apply it no-opped onto the May table, then its unique index on the June-only column tenant_id errored. A CI-only DROP TABLE band-aid in ci.yml masked it, and a stale compliance test (audit_retention_test.go) asserted May columns, so it only passed because the CI drop left the May table live. App code (auditarchive/pg_repository.go) and the 20260625_08 immutability trigger both use the June shape, so June is authoritative.
fix: Made 20260625_06 self-healing (permitted: it was un-applied and always-failing): drop the stale May table and its May-era policies (manifest_service_role_all, manifest_auditor_select) then create the June table, with hive_app INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE and auditor_ro SELECT grants relocated in. Removed the CI DROP band-aid so CI validates the real chain. Fixed audit_retention_test.go to assert June columns. Stale May table provably empty everywhere (app writes June-only columns, so writes against the May shape always error; staging confirmed 0 rows), so the drop preserves all audit data. Validated: full migration chain applies cleanly on a fresh pgvector:pg17 with no drop hack, and the compliance + RLS suites pass against the June schema.

error_message: Desktop sandbox launch() could hang the whole app (once a 15+ minute cargo test hang) inside the Command::pre_exec closure
root_cause: The pre_exec closure ran after fork() and before execve() in a child of a multithreaded process but was not async-signal-safe: it built the Landlock ruleset (Ruleset build, PathFd::new), compiled the seccomp BPF program, ran codex pre_main_hardening (std::env::remove_var over vars_os), and used format! on error paths. Allocating in a forked child can deadlock forever if another thread held the allocator lock at fork, and std makes the parent spawn() block until the child execs or errors, so the parent hangs too.
fix: Hoist all allocation and fd setup before the fork: build_landlock_ruleset returns a RulesetCreated (converted to OwnedFd) and build_seccomp_filter returns the compiled BpfProgram, both in the parent. Strip LD_* env on the Command before fork instead of via std::env in the child. The closure now performs only raw async-signal-safe syscalls on pre-built values: prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE) via codex disable_process_dumping, setrlimit(RLIMIT_CORE), prctl(PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS), raw landlock_restrict_self on the pre-built fd, and seccompiler::apply_filter over the pre-compiled program; error paths map to allocation-free io::Errors. Added tests/launch_spawn.rs end-to-end regression guard. The #341 10s spawn timeout stays as defense in depth.

error_message: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "idx_request_attempts_account_request_attempt" (SQLSTATE 23505) on chat dispatch
root_cause: Non-idempotent request-attempt insert. A single edge-api chat request starts the same attempt twice for one (account_id, request_id, attempt_number=1): the orchestrator calls StartAttempt directly (status dispatching), then CreateReservation internally calls usage.StartAttempt again (accounting/service.go). usage/repository.go CreateAttempt used a plain INSERT, so the second insert hit the unique index and raised 23505. Non-fatal to the served request (errors were logged as non-fatal), but the error aborted the reservation transaction, silently dropping the credit hold, and polluted logs.
fix: Make CreateAttempt idempotent with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (account_id, request_id, attempt_number) DO UPDATE SET status = request_attempts.status RETURNING ... The no-op SET returns the pre-existing attempt (first write wins); status transitions stay owned by UpdateAttemptStatus so an attempt never moves backward. Preserves append-only semantics and money-path correctness (single attempt, single reservation, no double-charge). Added DB-backed regression test TestCreateAttemptIsIdempotentOnAccountRequestAttempt in apps/control-plane/internal/usage/repository_test.go asserting no 23505, same row returned, exactly one row.

error_message: agent-subsystem /v1 endpoints (/v1/rag/*, /v1/agent/tasks*, /v1/artifacts*) 404 via UnsupportedEndpointMiddleware; entire agent-subsystem web surface dead (demo blocker)
root_cause: support matrix supported_now never updated for Waves 2-4 endpoints. The edge-api UnsupportedEndpointMiddleware 404s any /v1/ path not marked supported_now in packages/openai-contract/matrix/support-matrix.json (loaded at boot, baked into the Docker image). The rag/agent/artifacts handlers shipped wired and feature-gated but were only covered by per-package isolation tests that bypass the full middleware chain, so CI stayed green while every request 404-ed in a real stack. Note: support-matrix.json is the hand-maintained source; overlays/hive-support-status.yaml is an OpenAI-only OpenAPI overlay consumed by nothing and does not feed the matrix.
fix: Add supported_now entries for the 13 real proprietary routes (verified against the router registrations, not the ticket's guide) to support-matrix.json, then regenerate docs/support-matrix.md + generated/hive-openapi.yaml via generate-matrix.sh. Add apps/edge-api/internal/middleware/unsupported_integration_test.go, a full-chain integration test that drives all 13 paths through the real UnsupportedEndpointMiddleware + the real committed matrix: 404 before, 200 after.

error_message: CI job 'Egress firewall e2e (bwrap)' failed deterministically: ALLOWED probe (127.0.0.2) returned '502 CONNECT tunnel failed' instead of 200 (disallowed 403 and direct-refused were fine). Passed locally because only the Rust unit tests were run, never the shell e2e, which executes only in CI where HIVE_EGRESS_E2E_REQUIRE=1.
root_cause: egress-proxy-harness spawned AllowlistProxy via spawn(), which forces allow_local_dest=false. The e2e uses two loopback IPs (127.0.0.2 allowed vs 127.0.0.3 denied) as a throwaway stand-in internet. For the allowed target, is_allowed passes but resolve_pinned then hits the is_forbidden_ip loopback guard (all of 127.0.0.0/8 is loopback), returns Err, and the handler writes 502 Bad Gateway before dialing. No non-forbidden address answers on a CI runner, so the allowed probe could never reach 200 with that harness. Not a bwrap or allowlist-logic bug.
fix: Add pub AllowlistProxy::spawn_allowing_local_dest (test-only wrapper over spawn_with_policy(..., true), the same opt-out the proxy's own unit tests use) and call it from the egress-proxy-harness example. Relaxes only the redundant destination-IP guard (separately unit-tested); the allowlist host check and netns isolation the e2e asserts stay unchanged. Verified: raw CONNECT over the socket gives allowed=200 / disallowed=403, and the full scripts/egress-bwrap-e2e.sh passes with HIVE_EGRESS_E2E_REQUIRE=1 inside a real bwrap sandbox (allowed=200, disallowed=403, direct refused).

error_message: apptainer build agent-engine.sif FATAL in %post: '/usr/local/bin/python3: No module named playwright' at 'python3 -m playwright install --with-deps chromium'; exit status 1 (CI job Build agent-engine.sif, PR #351)
root_cause: The vendored trio (openhands-sdk/-tools/-workspace) is installed with pip --no-deps to protect the patched workspace. That also drops openhands-tools' declared third-party runtime deps (binaryornot, cachetools, libtmux, browser-use, func-timeout, tom-swe). browser-use is what pulls playwright. openhands-agent-server is installed with deps but does not depend on openhands-tools, so pip never backfilled them (an already-installed --no-deps package is treated as satisfied, its missing deps never resolved). The subsequent playwright CLI invocation then failed because playwright was never installed.
fix: In deploy/apptainer/agent-engine.def %post, after the trio and agent-server installs and before 'playwright install', add an explicit 'pip install' of openhands-tools' third-party runtime deps (binaryornot>=0.4.4, cachetools, libtmux>=0.53.0, browser-use>=0.8.0, func-timeout>=4.3.5, tom-swe>=1.0.3). These are plain PyPI packages, not the vendored trio, so the patched trio is left untouched (pip sees them already satisfied). Mirrors vendor/openhands/openhands-tools/pyproject.toml dependencies; keep in step with it.

error_message: docker compose --profile tools run toolchain bash -c "..." exits 0 with zero output, tests silently not run
root_cause: toolchain image is Alpine with no bash and ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/sh","-c"]; wrapping with bash -c or sh -c double-wraps so the nested shell reads EOF and exits 0 without executing
fix: pass the command string directly as the single arg: docker compose --profile tools run toolchain "cd /workspace && go test ..."; CLAUDE.md testing section updated 2026-07-19

error_message: https://console-hive.scubed.co/ returned HTTP 200 with Content-Length 0 (no body, no redirect) through the Cloudflare Tunnel right after the self-hosted web-console cutover (PR #456); web-console-prod itself worked fine when curled directly inside the box
root_cause: Caddyfile.console's site address is http://{$CONSOLE_DOMAIN:console.localhost}, a Host-matched site block. The box's .env never set CONSOLE_DOMAIN or CONSOLE_EXTERNAL_SCHEME (PR #456 introduced the vars but the box's .env predated the PR), so Caddy only matched Host: console.localhost. Cloudflare Tunnel and any real client send Host: console-hive.scubed.co, which matched no site block; Caddy's fallback response for an unmatched Host in this build is 200 empty, not 404 or connection refused, which made the failure look like a working-but-blank origin instead of a routing miss.
fix: Append CONSOLE_DOMAIN=console-hive.scubed.co and CONSOLE_EXTERNAL_SCHEME=https to the box's .env (matching the existing HIVE_CHAT_EXTERNAL_SCHEME/ARTIFACTS_DOMAIN pattern), then docker compose --env-file ../../.env up -d --force-recreate caddy-console to pick up the new env at container-create time (a plain restart does not re-resolve compose env substitution). Verified end to end: https://console-hive.scubed.co/ -> 307 to /auth/sign-in -> 200 Hive Console page.

error_message: Every password grant for a user with no ACTIVE public.tenant_users row returned HTTP 500 with {"code":"P0001","message":"no_active_membership"}. Sign-up succeeded, first sign-in then failed permanently. 11 of 19 live users were stranded, 92 occurrences in 24 hours. The sign-in and OAuth consent forms rendered the raw upstream string 'Error running hook URI: pg-functions://postgres/public/custom_access_token_hook' to unauthenticated visitors.
root_cause: Two faults stacked. First, public.custom_access_token_hook did RAISE EXCEPTION 'no_active_membership' whenever no ACTIVE tenant_users row joined to a non-archived tenant resolved, which denied the user the very request that would provision them, so the state was unrecoverable from the client. Second, and the reason such users existed at all, public.tenant_users was written by exactly one caller: apps/control-plane/internal/signup/webhook.go at POST /internal/auth/user-created, driven by a Supabase Database Webhook on auth.users insert. That webhook is dashboard state, not repository state, and it had never been created on the live project. A query for triggers on auth.users and for any supabase_functions.http_request trigger returned zero rows, so no signup had ever produced a membership. The demo owner only worked because scripts/seed-demo-owner.py had inserted their row directly. A third, separate fault surfaced while auditing the inert-token invariant: apps/control-plane/internal/auth/client.go read the tenant from user_metadata.selected_tenant_id, which GoTrue lets the user write via PUT /auth/v1/user, and never validated it against an ACTIVE membership the way the token hook does, so any signed-in caller could assert an arbitrary tenant id and read another tenant's model visibility list through /api/v1/catalog/models (OptionalRequire, not admin gated).
fix: New migration supabase/migrations/20260727_01_token_hook_membershipless_no_raise.sql replaces the RAISE with an early return of the unmodified claims, so a membership-less user receives a valid token carrying no tenant_id, tenants, role or owui_role claim. Absent, never null, so no consumer can read the key and treat null as a wildcard. The member path is byte-for-byte unchanged including the owui_role OWNER to ADMIN remap. Resolution and the membership write were extracted from webhook.go into signup.Provisioner.Reconcile (apps/control-plane/internal/signup/reconcile.go), the single implementation both entry points now call; the webhook keeps working for deployments that do have the Database Webhook. A new authenticated route POST /api/v1/viewer/tenant-provision (apps/control-plane/internal/signup/viewer_http.go) lets the console reconcile on the first request from a tenant-less user; it derives identity solely from auth.ViewerFromContext, decodes no body, and accepts neither a tenant id nor an invite token, so a caller cannot name anybody or anything. Idempotency comes from an existing-ACTIVE-membership short-circuit plus the tenant_users (tenant_id, user_id) primary key with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; Reconcile never creates a tenant in either deployment posture, so no race can produce two. The escalation was closed with auth.Client.WithMembershipCheck, wired in main.go to tenantMembershipCheck(pool), which validates the self-asserted tenant against the same ACTIVE-and-not-archived predicate the hook uses and collapses anything unverified to uuid.Nil. Tests: 4 hook tests (static guard plus live-DB member, membership-less and revoked claim assertions), 9 reconcile and endpoint tests including an 8-way concurrency race and a body-cannot-name-a-user security test, 6 control-plane escalation tests, and 3 edge-api inert-token tests covering absent, empty, null, unparseable, all-zero and wrong-type tenant claims. Sanitization of the raw hook string is owned by the web-console client boundary (lib/auth/auth-error.ts), because GoTrue's error text is upstream and web-console is the last hop before the browser.

error_message: A tenant could invoke any routed model alias regardless of the per-tenant model visibility an admin had configured. tenant_model_visibility was consulted only when listing the catalog; POST /v1/chat/completions resolved a route for a hidden alias and streamed a normal completion. Compounding it, /internal/catalog/visibility/* answered 404, so the admin control had no reachable write path at all.
root_cause: Enforcement lived in the catalog listing query (catalog/repository.go ListAliasesForTenant) instead of in the path that grants access. edge-api chat dispatch called SelectRoute with only AliasID plus capability flags and never sent a tenant, and routing/service.go aliasAllowed returns true for an empty allowlist, so the empty list meant allow-all. /v1/models served the global ListPublicAliases snapshot for the same reason. Separately, catalog.NewVisibilityHandler was never constructed in control-plane cmd/server/main.go, so router.go skipped mounting the admin visibility routes.
fix: Extracted the verdict into catalog.AliasVisibleToTenant and made it the single decider: one query (tenantVisibilityQuery) with an optional alias filter feeds one predicate, so ListAliasesForTenant and the new IsAliasVisibleToTenant cannot disagree. routing.Service takes a required TenantEntitlements dependency and refuses tenant-scoped selections for unentitled aliases with ErrModelNotEntitled (403), failing closed when the dependency is nil. edge-api RoutingClient.SelectRoute binds the tenant from auth.TenantID(ctx) and discards any caller-supplied value, so every JWT inference path (chat, RAG, audio, images) is covered at one seam. /v1/models reads a new tenant-scoped snapshot endpoint for JWT sessions. Mounted the visibility admin handler. Added tools/lint-tenant-model-visibility-single-source.mjs so a second copy of the rules cannot be written outside the catalog package. Empty-means-allow for public and preview aliases was preserved deliberately: tenant_model_visibility is empty on every deployment, so deny-by-default would have revoked chat for every tenant.

error_message: https://console-hive.scubed.co/auth/callback returned 307 with Location: https://0.0.0.0:3000/console, and https://chat-hive.scubed.co/agent-workspace/auth/callback returned 307 with Location: https://0.0.0.0:3000/agent-workspace/auth/sign-in. Users completing email verification or an OAuth code exchange landed on a dead host (ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED) instead of the console.
root_cause: Next.js does not build a request's URL from the Host header. With experimental.trustHostHeader unset, resolve-routes.js composes initUrl from the server's OWN bind address: `${protocol}://${formatHostname(opts.hostname || 'localhost')}:${opts.port}${req.url}`, and formatHostname('0.0.0.0') returns it verbatim. Both console containers start with `--hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 3000`, and Caddy/Cloudflare Tunnel supply the scheme via X-Forwarded-Proto, so any route handler resolving an absolute redirect against request.url emitted https://0.0.0.0:3000. The helper for this already existed: PR #157 added apps/web-console/lib/http/origin.ts, whose header comment documents this exact trap, but wired it into only 2 of 5 call sites. A second, compounding cause: the helper preferred NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL unconditionally, and .env.example ships http://localhost:3000, so a deployment carrying that value forward would have emitted localhost redirects and mailed localhost verification links.
fix: Wired resolveCanonicalOrigin into the three remaining call sites: apps/web-console/app/auth/callback/route.ts, apps/web-console/app/console/account-switch/route.ts (all four targets), and apps/agent-console/app/auth/callback/route.ts (keeping PR #438's BASE_PATH prefix). Query params now come from request.nextUrl.searchParams, which derives from the request line and is unaffected. Corrected the helper's precedence: a loopback NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is demoted below X-Forwarded-Host/Host while a real configured origin still outranks every header (preserving PR #157's anti-spoofing property), and wildcard bind addresses plus unparseable hosts are rejected from every source. agent-console got its own copy of the helper (separate npm package, separate Docker build context, so no shared import is possible) and needed no new build arg. Did NOT use experimental.trustHostHeader: it hardcodes https:// and pastes in the raw attacker-reachable Host header, which is the open-redirect shape origin.ts exists to prevent. Added tools/lint-no-request-url-origin.mjs, which fails CI if any route handler in either app reads request.url or nextUrl.origin, or if the two helper copies drift apart. Middleware is deliberately out of scope: verified live that Next.js emits a relative Location for a same-origin middleware redirect, so both middlewares are correct despite using the same expression. Proven live before/after with the real Dockerfiles behind the real Caddy configs; transcript and browser captures in docs/proof/console-origin-2026-07-27/.

error_message: /console/settings/billing returned HTTP 500 with a bare Next.js digest page and no recovery for any account that has zero rows in public.account_profiles (7 of 18 accounts on the dev project). Server-side throw: Error: profile not found at getBillingProfile (lib/control-plane/client.ts) from BillingSettingsPage's Promise.all.
root_cause: profiles/repository.go GetBillingProfile inner-joined public.account_profiles while every column it selects is already COALESCEd against that table being absent, so a missing profile row produced pgx.ErrNoRows, mapped to ErrNotFound, and returned 404. web-console getBillingProfile threw on any non-OK response (its sibling getAccountProfile already special-cased 404), and there was no error.tsx anywhere under apps/web-console/app, so the throw escaped to the bare digest page.
fix: Three layers. 1) LEFT JOIN public.account_profiles in GetBillingProfile so a profile-less account gets the coalesced empty profile (legal_entity_type falls back to individual or private_company by account_type); only a missing account is not-found. 2) getBillingProfile returns an empty billing profile on 404, mirroring getAccountProfile; other statuses still throw. 3) Added apps/web-console/app/console/error.tsx, the app's first error boundary, with an EmptyState and a working reset. Also split the 403 on this endpoint so a verified non-owner gets owner_role_required instead of the false email_verification_required. Verified live: pre-fix control-plane returns 404 and the page 500s, post-fix returns 200 with empty values and the page renders. Live-Postgres repository tests added and ./internal/profiles/... wired into the live-DB CI step.

error_message: https://artifacts-hive.scubed.co/ returns HTTP 308 with Location pointing back at itself, infinite redirect loop, curl -L hits 50-redirect cap
root_cause: deploy/docker/Caddyfile.artifacts used a bare-hostname site address ({$ARTIFACTS_DOMAIN:artifacts.localhost} {), which triggers Caddy's automatic-HTTPS + HTTP-to-HTTPS auto-redirect. Behind Cloudflare Tunnel (or any external TLS terminator), the origin only ever receives plain HTTP, so Caddy redirects every request to https://<same-host>/ forever. A first-pass fix to bare `:80 {` stopped the loop but removed Caddy's host-header matching entirely, turning the container into a catch-all that would serve /artifacts/* content under ANY Host header -- a real regression against this file's own documented origin-isolation invariant (artifacts must stay on a separate origin from the chat/main-app domain so browser same-origin policy protects cookies). Caught by CodeRabbit + a second review bot on PR #434 before merge.
fix: Use an explicit scheme in the site address instead: http://{$ARTIFACTS_DOMAIN:artifacts.localhost} { ... }. Caddy's automatic-HTTPS is triggered by the ABSENCE of an explicit scheme, not by the presence of a hostname -- naming http:// disables auto-HTTPS/redirect while keeping host-header matching intact. Fixed in PR #434 (sakibsadmanshajib/hive), merged 2026-07-26. Verified live against a real Cloudflare-Tunnel-fronted deployment both ways: correct Host = reaches reverse_proxy (no redirect); wrong Host = empty response, artifact content never served.

error_message: After `git pull` on a deployed box, a fixed Caddyfile still served the OLD behavior even after `docker compose build` + `up -d --no-deps` + `docker exec caddy reload`
root_cause: Caddyfile.* is a single-file bind mount into the caddy-owui/caddy-artifacts containers (image is upstream caddy:2-alpine, no build step). `git pull` writes a NEW inode for the file; Docker's bind mount was already resolved to the OLD inode at container start, so neither `build` (no-op, nothing to build) nor a plain `up -d` (container already Running, not recreated) nor an in-container `reload` (re-reads the stale mounted path) pick up the new content.
fix: Any Caddyfile-only change on a running box needs `docker compose ... up -d --no-deps --force-recreate <service>` specifically -- not build, not a bare up, not exec reload.

error_message: Sign-in to https://chat-hive.scubed.co/agent-workspace succeeded but the browser landed on Open WebUI's login page (/auth?redirect=%2Ftasks) instead of the Cowork task console
root_cause: page.tsx called window.location.assign("/tasks"). Next.js applies basePath to its own primitives (next/link, useRouter, next/navigation redirect) but NOT to raw URLs given to window.location.* or NextResponse.redirect. The bare /tasks fell outside Caddy's /agent-workspace/* matcher, so Open WebUI's catch-all reverse_proxy answered it. app/auth/callback/route.ts had the same defect on both NextResponse.redirect targets. middleware.ts had already hit this and prefixed its own redirects, making this the third occurrence of one mistake.
fix: Extracted the literal to apps/agent-console/lib/base-path.ts and imported BASE_PATH in all three call sites (middleware.ts, sign-in page, callback route). Regression tests: app/auth/sign-in/page.test.tsx, app/auth/callback/route.test.ts. PR #438.

error_message: Task console showed "Could not load tasks." with 10 browser CORS errors: no Access-Control-Allow-Origin on https://api-hive.scubed.co/v1/agent/tasks from origin https://chat-hive.scubed.co
root_cause: edge-api implements NO CORS middleware at all (zero Access-Control-* headers anywhere in apps/edge-api). agent-console's task console fetches /v1/agent/tasks from the BROWSER using NEXT_PUBLIC_EDGE_API_BASE_URL, set to the api host while the page is served from the chat host, so every list, create and cancel died in preflight. This never worked in a browser in any environment, including local dev (default base http://localhost:8080 against a page on :3003). Unit tests mock fetch, so they never caught it.
fix: Avoided opening a CORS surface on the gateway. Routed /v1/agent/* through the same Caddy listener that already fronts agent-console and built agent-console with NEXT_PUBLIC_EDGE_API_BASE_URL empty, so the client baseUrl falls back to "" and fetches are relative and same-origin. Auth unchanged, edge-api still validates the Supabase bearer token. PR #438.

error_message: Supabase login returned 400 Invalid login credentials for demo@hive-demo.invalid using a password seed-demo-owner.py had printed seconds earlier
root_cause: seed-demo-owner.py generates a fresh random password on EVERY run. It is idempotent for the tenant, role and feature-gate rows but not for the password. With several agents running it concurrently against one box, each run rotates the password out from under the others, so everyone sees Invalid login credentials even with a just-printed password.
fix: Stopped relying on the shared account for concurrent verification: created a dedicated user with a stable password, granted tenant OWNER on the same demo tenant via tenant_users. For the shared account, reset a stable password through the Supabase admin API and told other agents to stop re-running the seed.

error_message: POST /v1/messages dispatched a caller-supplied model straight to LiteLLM, so a raw route id such as route-groq-fast reached a provider with no alias resolution, no per-tenant entitlement check, no API-key alias allowlist check and no credit reservation
root_cause: The Anthropic surface built its own upstream dispatch instead of delegating to the wired /v1/chat/completions chain. LiteLLM model names ARE route ids (deploy/litellm/config.yaml declares its model_list entries as route-openrouter-default, route-groq-fast and so on), so forwarding the client model unresolved let a caller address a route directly and skip every control that hangs off routing.Service.SelectRoute plus the whole accounting lifecycle. Two adjacent defects kept it latent and would have made it live: /v1/messages was never registered in the support matrix so UnsupportedEndpointMiddleware 404d it before the handler ran, and the chat dispatcher re-marshalled a three-field struct which silently dropped max_tokens, temperature, tools and stream_options.
fix: Gave the handler a single dependency, the wired POST /v1/chat/completions handler chain, and made it translate and delegate: alias resolution, entitlement, the API-key allowlist, credit reservation and settlement, retry, tracing and audit are reused rather than duplicated. Response translation moved into a ResponseWriter that translates SSE incrementally, folds a stream back into one message for a non-streaming caller, and forwards a non-2xx response unchanged since the delegated chain already sanitizes it. Always dispatch downstream as a stream with stream_options.include_usage so the reservation settles at real token counts. Registered both Messages endpoints in the support matrix and stopped the chat dispatcher dropping caller fields. Guards: tools/lint-litellm-dispatch-requires-routing.mjs plus a Go structural test, both failing when an edge-api package dispatches to LiteLLM without SelectRoute.

error_message: gh pr checks showed required contexts such as Go tests (control-plane) passing in 2 to 4 seconds on pull requests where those jobs genuinely take minutes, making the merge gate unreliable as a signal
root_cause: ci.yml was path filtered on the trigger, and a workflow skipped by a trigger path filter never creates its check runs, so required checks stayed Pending and blocked the merge. The workaround was ci-noop.yml, a second workflow that fired on the inverse paths-ignore set and published job names identical to ci.yml's as echo steps. GitHub runs a paths-ignore workflow whenever ANY changed file falls outside the ignore set, so a pull request touching both code and docs fired both workflows and each required context received two check runs, one real and one echo. The repository's visual-proof rule commits screenshots under docs/ alongside code, so that mixed shape is the common case. Proven live on PR #559 commit d05b7ba1: every required context had two check runs, ci.yml run 30301329356 taking 13s to 2m38s and ci-noop.yml run 30301329536 taking 2s to 4s.
fix: Deleted ci-noop.yml. Removed the trigger path filters from ci.yml and moved the decision into a leading changes job that lists the changed files through the GitHub API and emits one boolean. Jobs publishing a required check name use if: always() with per-step gating so they always report their own conclusion, which avoids depending on how branch protection treats a check run whose conclusion is skipped; non-required jobs use a plain job-level if:. The allow-list polarity is inverted so anything unrecognized, an API error, or an event with no diff runs the full suite, and any changed file with an executable extension runs the full suite regardless of directory. Removed the web-e2e-shim job, the last remaining pair of jobs sharing a check name, and added .github/ci/lint-workflow-check-names.mjs to the repo policy lints. The lint expands matrix job names against the real matrix values instead of a wildcard, so it fails on a duplicate producer for a required context, on a required context with no producer at all, and on a required job that can be skipped or whose workflow carries trigger path filters.

error_message: https://cp-hive.scubed.co returned HTTP 522 (origin connection timeout) on every path (/, /health, /healthz, /v1/health) while hive-control-plane-1 was Up and healthy on the box and api-hive.scubed.co/health returned 200 throughout
root_cause: cp-hive.scubed.co was a leftover proxied A record pointing at 40.233.86.19, the retired 1GB VM that docker-compose.staging.yml was written for. It had NO Cloudflare Tunnel ingress rule, so it was never served by the demo box at all: Cloudflare kept trying to open a connection to a dead origin and timed out with 522. The control-plane was healthy the whole time under control-hive.scubed.co, the hostname the web-console Worker actually uses. The mapping was invisible to review because cloudflared on the box runs 'tunnel run' with only a TUNNEL_TOKEN and no --config, so the tunnel is remotely managed and its ingress lived only in the Cloudflare dashboard. Review of the first fix found the more dangerous half of the same defect: the value that feeds payment callbacks does not come from the staging overlay at all, since nothing references that file. It comes from docker-compose.yml, which defaulted CONTROL_PLANE_PUBLIC_URL to http://localhost:8081. resolveCallbackBaseURL already derives the callback base from the request Host when the variable is empty, which behind the tunnel yields the correct public hostname, so the compose default guaranteed the variable was always set and the correct fallback could never run. Live payment providers would have received an unreachable loopback callback URL.
fix: Deleted the stale A record (zone record id 42db291d707ca4378f7c8efdc14ad773) so the name fails resolution instead of hanging. Brought the hostname map into the repo as deploy/cloudflare/tunnel-ingress.json plus deploy/cloudflare/reconcile-tunnel-dns.mjs, wired as npm run cloudflare:check and cloudflare:apply. Dropped the docker-compose.yml default for CONTROL_PLANE_PUBLIC_URL so the host-derived Go fallback runs, and documented the variable in .env.example. Labelled docker-compose.staging.yml as unreferenced and superseded. Extended apps/web-console/tests/unit/control-plane-host.test.ts to scan every tracked text file under deploy/ and fail on any scubed.co hostname that tunnel-ingress.json does not declare, which is the credential-free guard that would have caught this on the PR that introduced it.

error_message: Paying customer lands on raw webhook JSON (SSLCommerz) or a 404 (Stripe) after completing payment
root_cause: A payment rail has two outbound URLs that were conflated. SSLCommerz success_url/fail_url/cancel_url were set to CallbackBaseURL + /webhooks/sslcommerz/{success,fail,cancel}, which is the control-plane IPN handler, so the browser got {"status":"ok"} and a browser request could reach settlement. Stripe built ${CallbackBaseURL}/checkout/stripe?client_secret=..., a route present in no service. Both used the control-plane origin for a customer-facing landing page. Separately, deploy/docker/docker-compose.yml injected CONTROL_PLANE_PUBLIC_URL=http://localhost:8081 as a default, so the correct request-host fallback in resolveCallbackBaseURL never ran and providers were handed an unreachable callback base.
fix: Split InitiateInput into CallbackBaseURL (control-plane, webhooks and settlement only) and ReturnBaseURL (console, browser only). ReturnBaseURL resolves from WEB_CONSOLE_PUBLIC_URL then NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, with no hardcoded default, so a missing value refuses the checkout loudly instead of stranding a payer. Stripe moved to a hosted Checkout Session so both rails share one shape. Added one console return page with success/pending/failure/cancelled read from the payment intent via a new GET-only account-scoped endpoint; query params are never trusted as state. Removed the three SSLCommerz browser routes from the webhook surface. resolveCallbackBaseURL now demotes a loopback CONTROL_PLANE_PUBLIC_URL below the real request host.

error_message: Invitation acceptance impossible for a signed-out invitee: /auth/sign-in?next=/invitations/accept dropped the ?token, and later a member hitting /console/members hit the console error boundary while an already-member acceptance returned an opaque 500
root_cause: The acceptance page built its sign-in bounce from a bare path and lib/auth/next-target.ts allow-listed /invitations/accept as an exact match only, so any query string collapsed to /console. Separately the accept handler mapped every service error to 400 with the raw internal string, the members page never read its own searchParams so invite feedback was computed and discarded, getMembers threw a bare Error on the owner-only 403 so a member crashed the page, and AcceptInvitation wrote the membership without checking for an existing one, surfacing the unique-constraint violation as a server error
fix: Read the token before the auth check and carry it in next via appendNextParam; move /invitations/accept from the exact allow-list to the prefix arm beside /oauth/consent so path?query matches but /invitations/accept-evil still does not; map acceptance failures to stable codes (expired 410, already accepted 409, already member 409, email mismatch 403, not found 404) and render distinct truthful copy with a real next action for each; render invited/joined/role_updated/error searchParams as a status or alert banner; detect an existing membership before the write; catch the 403 from getMembers as an owner-only explanation and rethrow anything else; add a role selector at invite time, per-row role editors, member emails instead of UUIDs, and a PATCH /api/v1/accounts/current/members/{user_id} route gated on members.manage with no-self-change and last-owner guards enforced in the service and again in the UPDATE statement

error_message: sqlalchemy.exc.ProgrammingError: (psycopg2.ProgrammingError) invalid dsn: invalid connection option "pool_max_conns"
root_cause: PR #593 appended pool_max_conns to the shared Supabase DSNs. pool_max_conns is a pgx (Go) connection-string parameter, not a libpq one. Open WebUI connects via SQLAlchemy + psycopg2, which parses the DSN with libpq make_dsn and rejects any unknown option, so open-webui failed its healthcheck 19s after start and deploy-demo-box step Rebuild + recreate changed services failed. control-plane and edge-api both use pgx and went Healthy in the same run, which is why only chat-hive returned 502.
fix: Keep pool_max_conns only on the pgx service DSNs (control-plane, edge-api). Give open-webui a clean libpq DSN with no pgx-only options; size its pool with Open WebUI env vars instead.

error_message: PR #606 review: control-plane persisted raw err.Error() from agent-engine Launch failures into the customer-visible task error_message field
root_cause: Service.CreateTask default branch (any Launch error besides ErrEngineNotConfigured) returned s.repo.Transition(...,err.Error()) directly, so an arbitrary Engine implementation error (dial failure with internal hostname, provider error body, etc.) could reach the task record returned by http.go taskResponse. ErrEngineNotConfigured already had a sanitized message (engineUnavailableMessage); the generic path never got the same treatment.
fix: Added engineLaunchFailedMessage fixed string, same pattern as engineUnavailableMessage. Default branch now logs the real error via slog.Default().WarnContext (task_id + error) then persists the generic message, mirroring the existing poller.go sanitization pattern for engine status-check failures. No error_code field exists on Task/http.go yet, so a machine-readable code was deferred (would need a schema migration) rather than added here.

error_message: Mid-stream client disconnect settled nothing: no charge, no ledger entry, no usage event, reservation stuck active forever
root_cause: executeStreaming/executeResponsesStreaming called FinalizeReservation with the same ctx the HTTP handler uses for the whole request. A client disconnect cancels that ctx, so accounting_client.go build the outbound request via http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, ...) and it failed before leaving the process. The tail settle block then set finalized = true unconditionally regardless of whether the call actually succeeded, which suppressed the existing deferred release path too. Separately, the terminal-usage-missing fallback charged a hardcoded flat 10000 estimate (chat_completions.go / completions.go), a latent overcharge whenever no real usage block arrived.
fix: Collapsed settlement into the one existing defer (already runs on every exit) via a new settleStream helper that always dispatches on context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second), independent of the caller ctx a disconnect cancels. Deleted the tail settle block and its flat-10000 fallback; delivered tokens (usage-confirmed or, absent that, a content-based estimate, floored at 1 when anything was produced) settle via FinalizeReservation, nothing delivered releases in full via ReleaseReservation. finalized is set only after settleStream itself reports success, so a failed settle still falls through to the disconnect-release path on the next exit. terminal_usage_confirmed mirrors hasUsage so a content-estimate settle still routes to needs_reconciliation.

error_message: PR #602's own fix still stranded holds and undercharged: three dispatch-failure branches released on the cancelled request context and discarded the error while forcing finalized=true anyway; recordCompletedEvent was skipped whenever CreateReservation had failed non-fatally; the no-confirmed-usage settlement estimate billed completion bytes only, ignoring prompt cost; and usage_events inserts for the new upstream_error/finalize_failed/interrupted event types were silently rejected by a stale CHECK constraint.
root_cause: Two independent reviewers on PR #602 found the settleStream fix from the first round did not cover every exit path: the three pre-SSE failure branches (dispatch error, non-2xx upstream status, missing http.Flusher) in both stream.go and stream_responses.go still called ReleaseReservation(ctx, ...) on the caller's request context (the same context a client disconnect cancels), discarded the returned error with `_ =`, and set finalized = true unconditionally -- reproducing the exact bug PR #602 exists to fix, just one step earlier in the lifecycle. Separately, settleStream's defer guard `if finalized || reservation.ID == ""` skipped recordCompletedEvent entirely whenever CreateReservation had failed non-fatally (an explicitly tolerated transient control-plane error), dropping completed-usage telemetry. settlementCredits' no-confirmed-usage fallback estimated completion tokens from streamed content only, so a client that disconnected right after the first output token billed roughly one credit regardless of prompt size, an abuse vector on a prepaid product since the client controls when to disconnect. Finally, usage_events.event_type's original CHECK constraint (20260330_02_usage_accounting.sql) never included upstream_error, finalize_failed, or interrupted, so recordInterruptedEvent's insert failed on every call and the error was discarded, hiding the gap.
fix: Added releaseReservationBackground(snapshot, reservationID, requestID, reason), a shared helper that releases on a fresh context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), accountingTimeout) and returns true only on real success; all six failure-branch sites (three per file) now gate finalized on that return value instead of assuming success, so a failed immediate release still falls through to the deferred settleStream retry. Removed the reservation.ID == "" short-circuit from both defer guards; settleStream now internally skips the ReleaseReservation/FinalizeReservation network calls when reservation.ID is empty but still calls recordInterruptedEvent or recordCompletedEvent so telemetry is never dropped just because CreateReservation failed. settlementCredits gained a promptBody parameter: when no confirmed usage exists but content was delivered, credits are now estimateCompletionTokens(promptBody) + estimateCompletionTokens(content), aligning the disconnect-estimate path with the confirmed path's prompt+completion billing (delivered stays gated on completion content only, so a true zero-content disconnect still releases in full). recordInterruptedEvent no longer discards RecordUsageEvent's error. Added migration 20260730_01_usage_events_event_type_extend.sql extending the CHECK constraint to include upstream_error, finalize_failed, and interrupted, idempotent via DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS + re-ADD. Judged the reported over-release window (finalize charges then FinalizeReservation itself errors, fallback release could double-credit) as already closed: control-plane's releaseLocked (apps/control-plane/internal/accounting/service.go) checks reservation.Status == ReservationStatusFinalized before touching the ledger and returns a PolicyError instead of releasing, and finalize/release both run under the same per-account WithAccountLock, so no code change was needed there.

error_message: Issue #592: resetProfilesAndInvitation deletes account_billing_profiles rows in a loop with no paired upsert immediately after, the same un-paired delete-then-write shape PR #583 already fixed for account_memberships and account_invitations
root_cause: Audited and dismissed, not a real bug. GetBillingProfile (apps/control-plane/internal/profiles/repository.go) LEFT JOINs account_billing_profiles and COALESCEs every column, so a missing row reads back blank, never ErrNotFound: nothing observes the deleted-but-not-yet-reinserted window as broken. There is also no concurrent reader of that window: every spec beforeEach calls the fixture CLI via execFileSync, which blocks synchronously until the child process exits, and playwright.config.ts pins workers 1, so no page load can ever run during this function. Account ids are namespaced per E2E_RUN_KEY so two CI jobs never touch the same row either. supabase/functions/e2e-fixtures/index.ts, the other file the issue asked to audit, no longer exists: seeding moved in-process in PR #583.
fix: Documented the audit conclusion as an inline comment above the account_billing_profiles delete loop in apps/web-console/tests/e2e/support/e2e-fixture-seed.mjs, referencing issue #592 directly, so the dismissal reasoning survives instead of living only in a PR body. No functional code change: the delete stays a bare delete on purpose. Revisit if playwright workers ever goes above 1 or the fixture CLI stops blocking synchronously.

error_message: CALL public.purge_metering_shadow_verdicts() fails with ERROR: invalid transaction termination
root_cause: CREATE PROCEDURE ... SET search_path = public, pg_temp wraps every CALL in an implicit sub-transaction (to restore the GUC afterward); a COMMIT inside the procedure body cannot terminate that wrapper transaction, so any procedure that both sets a config GUC via the CREATE PROCEDURE SET clause and issues COMMIT/ROLLBACK internally fails at the first COMMIT.
fix: Drop the SET search_path clause from the procedure. Every table reference inside was already fully schema-qualified (public.metering_shadow_verdicts, public.metering_shadow_verdicts_retention_config), so the clause bought nothing and removing it is free.

error_message: Re-running supabase/migrations/20260729_02_metering_shadow_verdicts_retention.sql a second time aborts with relation already exists
root_cause: CREATE TABLE public.metering_shadow_verdicts_retention_config had no IF NOT EXISTS guard while every other DDL statement in the same file did (extension, insert-on-conflict, create-or-replace-procedure), so the migration was not actually idempotent despite being written to look idempotent.
fix: Add IF NOT EXISTS to the CREATE TABLE statement.

error_message: PR #609 review: purge_metering_shadow_verdicts had no search_path pinning after the SET clause was deleted (not relocated) from CREATE PROCEDURE
root_cause: Postgres wraps a SET-clause procedure CREATE PROCEDURE ... SET search_path=... CALL in a sub-transaction to restore the setting afterward, and that wrapper rejects a COMMIT inside the body (invalid transaction termination). The earlier fix removed the SET clause outright to unblock the internal batch-loop COMMIT, leaving the procedure with an unpinned search_path (defense in depth gap) instead of relocating the pin.
fix: Move SET search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp; to the first statement inside the procedure body (mirrors the existing SET lock_timeout body-position pattern in the same procedure). Body-position SET coexists with the internal COMMIT. Verified live: two applies of both migrations with zero duplicate rows/errors, CALL with a forced multi-iteration batch size deletes stale rows and keeps fresh rows, and SHOW search_path in the same session reads pg_catalog, pg_temp immediately after CALL returns.

error_message: profile-completion.spec.ts billing settings save partial business profile fails intermittently in CI, roughly half the time, owner-only route 403 owner_role_required for the verified spec user
root_cause: seedAccountsAndMemberships writes verifiedUser two memberships (owner of primary workspace, member of shared workspace) in one multi-row upsert. account_memberships.created_at defaults to now() and one INSERT statement stamps every row with the same transaction timestamp, so the two rows tie on created_at. ListMembershipsByUserID (apps/control-plane/internal/accounts/repository.go) orders ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC, with id documented there as a tiebreaker only for that pathological same-created_at case. The bulk seed hits that case every run, so which row sorts first depends on comparing two freshly random gen_random_uuid() ids: a coin flip on every reseed. EnsureViewerContext takes memberships[0] as the default workspace on every specs first navigation, so about half of CI runs land the verified user in the member-role workspace and its owner-only route 403s.
fix: Stamped account_memberships.created_at explicitly in apps/web-console/tests/e2e/support/e2e-fixture-seed.mjs, one millisecond apart per array index in the seeds intended priority order (owned workspace before joined workspace), so the seeded rows never reach the tie case. Left the Go-side id tiebreak in ListMembershipsByUserID unchanged: it is correct general-purpose behavior for real simultaneous production writes and already has its own regression test (TestListMembershipsByUserID_TiebreaksByID), so the fix belongs at the seed source that manufactures the tie every run, not at the consumer that already resolves ties deterministically per call.

error_message: desktop entitlements tests: intermittent accept-thread stall and No rustls crypto provider is configured panic in cargo test
root_cause: mock_server test helper only tried listener.accept() once and silently dropped the connection handler thread on any transient accept error under CI load; separately, reqwest rustls-no-provider client construction panics unless a process-wide rustls CryptoProvider is installed first, which main.rs does at real startup but cargo test never runs main() and test order/parallelism is unspecified
fix: mock_server now loops on listener.incoming() retrying past transient accept errors instead of giving up after one Err; added a std::sync::Once-guarded ensure_crypto_provider() called from both mock_server and unreachable_origin so every fetch test installs rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider() before the first build_client() call regardless of run order

error_message: releaseLocked accepted a needs_reconciliation reservation, so a settled hold could be released a second time: released_credits was recomputed from an already-zero remaining hold, overwriting 8997 back to 0, flipping status away from needs_reconciliation, marking a charged and delivered attempt cancelled, and leaving a row where reserved != consumed + released
root_cause: the expand, finalize and release guards each enumerated the settled statuses they refused (a blocklist), so needs_reconciliation, added later for unconfirmed settlements, fell through the release and expand guards into the permitted path. Nothing consumes credit_reconciliation_jobs (issue 600), so those rows are terminal in practice and every one was a standing second-release target
fix: replaced the three blocklists with one allowlist predicate, reservationOpen, permitting only active and expanded, so an unrecognized or newly added status fails closed with a typed PolicyError (HTTP 409) instead of falling through. Money was never at risk: the release amount recomputed to 0 and the unified release idempotency key (PR 662) dedupes at the credit_idempotency_keys primary key regardless

error_message: audio billing charged flat hardcoded credits (1000 per speech request, 500 per transcription) and never read the model catalog, so a one second clip and a ten minute clip cost the same
root_cause: apps/edge-api/internal/audio/handler.go set EstimatedCredits/ActualCredits to literals at every reservation site. The package never consulted alias pricing at all: routing.SelectionResult carried Pricing but edge-api inference.SelectRouteResult did not decode it, and no field existed for a price unit. Speech and transcription are not token priced upstream (Groq bills per character and per hour of audio), so there was also no unit in which the catalog price could have been applied even if it had been read.
fix: Added model_aliases.price_unit (tokens|characters|seconds) with a CHECK that a non token unit prices only output_price_credits, repriced hive-tts and hive-stt from Groq published rates, carried pricing plus unit through routing.SelectionResult to inference.SelectRouteResult to audio.RouteResult, and derived every audio charge as quantity times catalog price via metering.ChargeCredits (per million units, math/big, round half up). Speech meters synthesized characters, transcription and translation meter audio seconds with the provider ten second minimum. The handler now asks upstream for verbose_json so a duration is always reported and reshapes the response back to the caller requested format; a 2xx with no duration is refused and the hold released rather than charged at a guess. An alias whose unit the endpoint cannot meter is refused before any hold is taken.

error_message: audio release-on-error sites released holds on the request context and discarded the error, so a disconnected client stranded the hold silently (#616 mechanism, most exposed at the new unpriceable-response refusal)
root_cause: every _ = h.accounting.ReleaseReservation(ctx, ...) in apps/edge-api/internal/audio/handler.go passed the request context. A release runs at the moment a request has already failed, which is when the client is most likely gone; a cancelled context aborts the accounting HTTP call before it is sent, and the dropped error hid the failure. settleReservation had already been fixed for finalize (#637) but the release sites were never converted.
fix: Added Handler.releaseHold in reservation.go: fresh context.Background with its own releaseTimeout, logs a failed release, and takes no context argument so a caller cannot pass a request context. Converted all fifteen release sites in handler.go. settleReservation untouched (already separate bounded contexts for finalize and fallback release). Three red-first tests in release_context_test.go assert the release context is live and bounded, that a failed release is logged, and that a cancelled request context still yields a live release context.

error_message: scripts/apply-migrations.sh seeded its baseline into public.hive_schema_migrations whenever that ledger was empty, so against a brand new database it recorded 61 of 84 migration files as already applied without executing any of them, then deployed against schema that was never created and reported success
root_cause: an empty ledger has two opposite meanings and looks identical in both: a database that predates the ledger and ran those migrations by hand, or a fresh database that has run nothing. The seed condition tested only the ledger, which cannot distinguish them, so the unknown state resolved to applied instead of to not applied
fix: apply-migrations.sh now calls probe-applied-migrations.py --baseline-state before seeding, which reads the schema and answers fresh, preexisting or ambiguous. Fresh skips the seed and runs the whole chain, preexisting seeds as before, ambiguous aborts with instructions and records nothing. HIVE_MIGRATION_BASELINE=seed|ignore is honoured only where the probe is inconclusive and is rejected when it contradicts the schema. Extensions are excluded from the decision because supabase/postgres ships pgcrypto and uuid-ossp pre-created. scripts/test-apply-migrations.sh proves the fresh case by counting executed migrations (84 of 84) against a real supabase/postgres 17.6.1.136

title: Chat, completions, responses and embeddings billed one credit per token, ignoring the alias catalog
error_message: credit_ledger_entries.usage_charge = -103 for a 72-input, 31-output request, exactly 72 + 31; hive-fast billed about 10.00 USD per million tokens against the 0.105 USD per million it carried in the catalog at the time, since repriced to 0.07 by PR #692. A 12000 input plus 3000 output request charged 15000 credits and settles at 118 credits at the live price ((12000 * 7000 + 3000 * 11200) / 1e6 = 117.6, round half up)
root_cause: settlementCredits in apps/edge-api/internal/inference/stream.go returned the provider's total_tokens as the credit figure, and both settlement sites (settleStream and executeSync) passed it through as FinalizeReservationInput.ActualCredits. model_aliases.input_price_credits and output_price_credits were never read on the text path. The correct per-million round-half-up math/big arithmetic existed in metering.ChargeCredits but only the audio path (PR #671) called it.
fix: Added apps/edge-api/internal/inference/pricing.go: CanPriceTokens gates on an explicit model_aliases.price_unit of tokens with at least one priced side, CreditsForTokens converts input and output counts through metering.ChargeCredits (single implementation, unchanged arithmetic) with a 1-credit floor, requireTokenPricing refuses a non-token-priced alias before any reservation exists. settlementCredits now takes the resolved route plus separate input and output token counts and returns its own confirmed verdict, so an unconfirmed estimate is catalog-priced too and a usage block reporting zero tokens is treated as absent rather than as a measured zero. settleStream carries the dispatched route. The JWT-session chat path records the same catalog figure in llm_traces.cost_credits.

error_message: deploy-demo-box reported success while no Caddyfile change ever reached the running proxy: PR #664 added a /v1/featuregate matcher to deploy/docker/Caddyfile.owui, run 30711940528 went fully green, and chat-hive.scubed.co kept answering /v1/featuregate with 200 text/html from Open WebUI
root_cause: Two stacked layers. First, each Caddyfile is a bind-mounted file, so changing its contents does not change the container specification and docker compose up -d finds nothing to recreate; Caddy keeps serving the config it parsed at startup and the deploy step exits 0 either way (hive-caddy-owui-1 was 32 hours old while edge-api and open-webui were 15 minutes old). Second, a single-file bind mount resolves to an inode at container start and git pull replaces the file by rename rather than editing in place, so the container's /etc/caddy/Caddyfile stays pinned to the old inode forever (host inode 133458 5216 bytes versus guest inode 174599 4665 bytes). That makes the obvious fix, caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile inside the container, re-read the stale copy and exit 0 having changed nothing.
fix: Added two steps to the deploy job in .github/workflows/deploy-demo-box.yml. The first validates each host Caddyfile by piping it into the container's caddy binary (caddy validate --config -), then compares the container's mounted copy with the host file: identical means an in-place caddy reload (zero downtime), different means the mount is inode-stale so the service is recreated with up -d --force-recreate --no-deps, which re-binds the mount and also stops the container reverting on its next restart. The second step asserts the outcome instead of trusting exit codes, probing localhost:3003/v1/featuregate and requiring an application/json body carrying a gateway shape, so a stale config fails the deploy instead of passing quietly. Verified live on the box: before 200 text/html, after 401 application/json UNAUTHENTICATED, with the four discriminator paths unchanged.

title: LiteLLM config sync SELECT referenced pr.model_id, a column that does not exist on provider_routes, failing on every invocation
error_message: ERROR: column pr.model_id does not exist (SQLSTATE 42703), from litellmconfig: sync: query routes
root_cause: SyncService.Sync (apps/control-plane/internal/litellmconfig/service.go) selected pr.model_id AS litellm_name and separately concatenated cp.litellm_prefix onto it. provider_routes has no model_id column (real columns: route_id, alias_id, provider, provider_model, litellm_model_name, price_class, health_state, priority), so the query errored unconditionally and no invocation of Sync ever wrote a config. The one test that exercised the real query, sync_integration_test.go, was gated behind LITELLM_TEST_DB_URL, which appeared nowhere under .github/, so it always skipped in CI and the defect shipped invisibly.
fix: Select pr.provider_model directly as litellm_name and drop the litellm_prefix concatenation: every seeded provider_routes row (openrouter, groq, nvidia_nim) already stores provider_model pre-prefixed (e.g. openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini), so concatenating cp.litellm_prefix would have double-prefixed it. Wired LITELLM_TEST_DB_URL into ci.yml go-tests bootstrap step against the same ephemeral pgvector/pgvector:pg17 service container used by HIVE_TEST_DB_URL/ROUTING_TEST_DB_URL, and added internal/litellmconfig/... to the -tags integration test invocation so this suite actually runs on every PR. Strengthened the test to assert every seeded active route appears in the generated model_list by model_name with the exact litellm_params.model it was seeded with, so a future column rename fails loudly instead of shipping an empty or wrong model list again.

error_message: TypeError: Failed to parse URL from /api/v1/accounts/current/api-keys/{id}/limits, web-console /console/api-keys/{id}/limits returned 500 for every key
root_cause: getKeyLimits/updateKeyLimits in apps/web-console/lib/api-keys.ts fetched a bare relative path through an injected fetch client. A React Server Component has no origin, so Node fetch rejects the URL before any request is made, and the helpers also carried no session bearer. The page additionally passed a fetch client object down to a Client Component, which is not a serialisable prop.
fix: Moved the transport into lib/control-plane/client.ts as getApiKeyLimits and updateApiKeyLimits, which use the existing getRequestContext (absolute CONTROL_PLANE_BASE_URL plus session headers). The page reads through the data layer and writes through an inline server action, so no fetch client crosses the Server/Client boundary and the 404 branch keys on ControlPlaneError.status instead of message text.

error_message: an unverified owner holding only api_keys.read got 403 on GET /api/v1/accounts/current/api-keys/{id}/limits and landed in the same React error boundary issue #552/#683 was filed to fix
root_cause: resolveViewerContext in apps/control-plane/internal/apikeys/http.go gated every api-keys route, including the read-only handleGetKey, handleListKeys and handleGetLimits, on authz.PermAPIKeysWrite, which requires RequiresVerified=true. authz.PermAPIKeysRead requires no verification, so an unverified owner was refused a permission the registry explicitly grants them.
fix: resolveViewerContext now takes an authz.Permission argument. Read handlers (handleGetKey, handleListKeys, handleGetLimits) pass authz.PermAPIKeysRead; mutating handlers keep authz.PermAPIKeysWrite. Added TestUnverifiedOwnerReadsLimitsButCannotWrite in limits_http_test.go: an unverified owner gets 200 on GET limits and 403 on PUT limits for the same principal.

error_message: npx playwright test --project=phase-19 exits 0 and reports only setup tests; all 7 per-push phase-19 spec files (tenant isolation, JWT expiry, cross-tenant attack, audit rows) are silently never collected, no error or warning
root_cause: apps/web-console/playwright.config.ts scoped the phase-19 project testMatch to a filename-only regex assuming Playwright tests it against the bare filename. Playwright actually tests testMatch regexes against the full absolute file path (runner/projectUtils.js collectFilesForProject), and an absolute path always contains path separators, so the anchored no-separator-from-position-0 pattern could never match any file. playwright test --list still exits 0 with zero collected specs and no diagnostic, the same silent-skip shape as issue 701.
fix: Rewrote testMatch to anchor on the phase-19 directory segment and stop before any further separator, so it matches the 7 direct-child spec files and deliberately excludes the e2e/phase-19/owui subtree, which is a separately configured nightly suite (own baseURL, own auth setup, documented in e2e/phase-19/README.md) that would otherwise get swept in under the wrong dependency chain. Added scripts/verify-phase19-collection.sh plus an npm script, which runs the real collector and fails loud if the project collection count is not exactly 7, verified to fail against the old regex and pass against the fix before commit. Did not wire --project=phase-19 into CI in this change: those specs need live Supabase auth and real upstreams whose pass state is unverified.

title: Five Go DB-backed/integration tests never executed in CI; two had fixture bugs making them impossible to pass on any real schema
error_message: catalog: insert or update on table "tenant_model_visibility" violates foreign key constraint "tenant_model_visibility_tenant_id_fkey" (SQLSTATE 23503). providers: null value in column "route_id" of relation "provider_routes" violates not-null constraint (SQLSTATE 23502).
root_cause: Same failure shape as #701/#705, repeated five times. TestDispatchHappyPathWritesLLMTraceAndAuditsChatRequest (edge-api/internal/chat) and the four TestTenantFallback_* tests (edge-api/internal/auth) had HIVE_TEST_DB_URL correctly wired at the CI job level, but the RLS step's edge-api package list omitted ./internal/chat/... and ./internal/auth/.... TestChatCompletions_ToolCapable_AllowsTools plus four siblings (edge-api/internal/inference) needed only -tags integration, which the edge-api leg never passed. TestTenantVisibilityIntegration (control-plane/internal/catalog) and TestProviderCRUDIntegration (control-plane/internal/providers) were gated behind CATALOG_TEST_DB_URL/PROVIDERS_TEST_DB_URL, neither wired anywhere under .github/, so they never ran; their fixtures also had never been proven against a real schema. The catalog test hardcoded tenant UUIDs a0000000.../b0000000... into tenant_model_visibility without ever inserting them into public.tenants, so the FK on tenant_id was never satisfiable. The providers test's raw provider_routes INSERT omitted route_id, a text primary key with no default, so the not-null constraint was never satisfiable.
fix: Fixture fixes only, no assertions weakened: added seedTenant to catalog_integration_test.go inserting tenantA/tenantB into public.tenants (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) before any visibility row references them, with cleanup; added an explicit route_id value (route-<slug>) to the provider_routes INSERT in providers/integration_test.go. CI wiring: added CATALOG_TEST_DB_URL and PROVIDERS_TEST_DB_URL to the existing ephemeral-Postgres bootstrap step (same DSN as HIVE_TEST_DB_URL/ROUTING_TEST_DB_URL/LITELLM_TEST_DB_URL); added ./internal/catalog/... and ./internal/providers/... to control-plane's -tags integration invocation; added -tags integration plus ./internal/chat/..., ./internal/auth/..., ./internal/inference/... to edge-api's RLS step. Added a CI=true loud t.Fatal (matching #705's precedent) to every connect/skip helper touched (catalog, providers, chat, auth) so a future missing env var fails the build instead of silently skipping again. apps/edge-api/internal/audio/live_voice_integration_test.go deliberately left untouched: its round trip needs a real GROQ_API_KEY and belongs in the paid live-integration lane, not this free job.

title: hive-default/hive-auto priced against paid models but OPENROUTER_DEFAULT_MODEL/OPENROUTER_AUTO_MODEL defaulted to OpenRouter's free-model router
error_message: provider_routes.provider_model read like the correct paid model (openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini, openrouter/openai/gpt-4.1-mini) while the box actually dispatched openrouter/free, an undisclosed arbitrary free model, so the catalog looked correct on audit while customers were billed the paid price for a free response.
root_cause: The model LiteLLM actually calls resolves at container start from an env var (deploy/litellm/config.yaml: model: os.environ/OPENROUTER_DEFAULT_MODEL / OPENROUTER_AUTO_MODEL), a mechanism completely independent of provider_routes.provider_model, which is descriptive metadata nothing in the dispatch path consults. .env.example defaulted both vars to openrouter/free with comments framing the free default as a deliberate cost-saving choice an operator opts out of, which is what made a real mispricing look intentional. No component compared the two, so the drift was invisible from the database alone.
fix: Live box state already corrected and verified by the owner (resolved model openai/gpt-4o-mini, 200 response, ledger charged 1 credit matching the catalog) before this PR. This PR prevents recurrence: .env.example now defaults OPENROUTER_DEFAULT_MODEL/OPENROUTER_AUTO_MODEL to the exact paid slugs provider_routes.provider_model names (matching comments corrected too), and deploy-demo-box.yml gained an 'Assert model catalog prices agree with the model LiteLLM will call' step that runs right after the recreate, queries provider_routes joined to model_aliases (price_unit='tokens', nonzero price, route not disabled/eol) via a disposable postgres:16-alpine psql container against the transaction-mode pooler DSN, reads LiteLLM's own GET /model/info (litellm_params.model is the env-var-substituted value per Router.set_model_list, not the os.environ/ template) and fails the deploy on any mismatch after stripping the leading provider/adapter segment from both sides (openrouter/ vs openai/ legitimately differ for hive-embedding-default's two routes, which use the openai/ generic adapter since LiteLLM's native openrouter/ provider does not map /embeddings). Proved locally with synthetic DB rows + /model/info payloads: the assertion logic fails (exit 1, correctly names both mispriced routes) against the openrouter/free state and passes (exit 0) against the fixed defaults, without falsely failing the multi-route embedding alias.

title: LiteLLM config sync reverted the embedding adapter workaround and dropped hand-tuned extra_body on every DB-managed route
error_message: No runtime error. The next admin provider sync would have written litellm_params.model: openrouter/nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-vl-1b-v2:free for route-openrouter-embedding (LiteLLM native openrouter/ provider does not map /embeddings, so RAG embeddings 404 upstream) and dropped extra_body.provider.allow_fallbacks/sort from route-openrouter-default and route-openrouter-auto.
root_cause: PR #705 restored SyncService.Sync ability to write the live /etc/litellm/config.yaml, and mergeConfig only preserved (a) whole model_list entries with no provider_routes row and (b) model_info on DB-managed entries. Generate built litellm_params from exactly {model, api_base, api_key} straight out of provider_routes.provider_model, so any hand-tuned key on a DB-managed entry (extra_body.provider tuning, added for the flaky usage-token root cause) was dropped, and the deliberate generic openai/ adapter used for embeddings (deploy/litellm/config.yaml section 5) was replaced by the routing-canonical openrouter/ prefix the DB stores.
fix: Two changes, no schema change and no new column. 1. Adapter awareness in the generator: SyncService.Sync now LEFT JOINs provider_capabilities and carries supports_embeddings into ModelEntry; litellmModel rewrites the leading provider segment to openai/ for an embeddings route, keeping the provider api_base, and Generate refuses an embeddings route with an empty api_base since openai/<model> without a base would send that provider key to api.openai.com. provider_routes.provider_model deliberately stays routing-canonical (openrouter/...) because the price catalog and deploy-demo-box.yml price assertion both read that column and canonicalize a live openai/X plus openrouter.ai api_base back to openrouter/X before comparing. 2. Field-level litellm_params preservation in mergeConfig: the generator owns model, api_base and api_key; every other key already present on the entry (and every other entry-level key, not just model_info) survives, mirroring the existing model_info rule.
verification: Both regression tests were written first and watched fail against origin/main on a live pgvector/pgvector:pg17 with the full migration chain applied: TestWriteAndRestartPreservesHandTunedLiteLLMParams (extra_body and timeout absent after sync) and TestSyncKeepsEmbeddingAdapterForSeededRoute (model emitted as openrouter/nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-vl-1b-v2:free). Both run in CI job Go tests (control-plane), the -short step and the -tags integration step respectively (LITELLM_TEST_DB_URL is wired into that job as of #705). Ad-hoc proof over a copy of the real deploy/litellm/config.yaml: after a sync the embedding entries carry openai/... plus the openrouter api_base, route-openrouter-default and route-openrouter-auto keep extra_body, route-doc-vlm and bge-m3 survive as orphans, litellm_settings and files_settings survive, and a replay of the deploy price assertion agrees on all 5 priced routes.

error_message: edge-api GET /v1/models answered 403 account_not_provisioned to the OWUI shim key that edge-api itself had just logged as active and able to authenticate model listing, RAG embeddings and TTS
root_cause: Two defects. (1) The shim key account had no public.tenant_billing_accounts row because scripts/seed-owui-e2e-user.py never wrote one, and PR #620 made API-key tenant resolution fail closed, so /v1/models 403s. (2) checkOWUIShimKey asserted a WEAKER predicate than the request path: it read snapshot.Status and the model allowlist but never snapshot.TenantID, the one field handleModels requires, so the boot log asserted the opposite of the truth and the outage stayed invisible behind a false green.
fix: Moved the tenant predicate onto authz.AuthSnapshot.TenantUUID and made all three consumers (handleModels, inference.Orchestrator.selectRoute, checkOWUIShimKey) call it, so probe and request path cannot drift. Probe failure now names the missing tenant_billing_accounts row and says a new key will not help. Seed script provisions the mapping before minting, refuses to repoint an existing one, and gained --tenant-slug because the mapping is 1:1 in both directions. Wired make test-scripts into the required repo-policy-lints CI job (nothing ran the python self-checks before) and made the nightly fail on a non-200 layer-2 status instead of printing 403 and exiting 0.

title: OWUI nightly Playwright suite 400s on native /api/v1/auths/signin for the OAuth-only seeded fixture user
error_message: open_webui.models.auths:authenticate_user: owui-e2e@hive-e2e.invalid followed by "POST /api/v1/auths/signin HTTP/1.1" 400, every nightly run since 2026-07-26
root_cause: Open WebUI OAuth signup (backend/open_webui/utils/oauth.py, pinned v0.10.2) creates every OAuth-provisioned local account with password=get_password_hash(str(uuid.uuid4())), commented "Random password, not used". The e2e fixture user is OAuth-only (ENABLE_SIGNUP false), so its Open WebUI account password is never known. 09-agent-workspace-launcher.spec.ts deliberately signs in via the native email/password form with the freshly rotated OWUI_E2E_PASSWORD, which can never match the random local password, so it always 400s regardless of volume age or password rotation timing. The leading hypothesis in #712 (owui-data volume persisting across nightly runs) was checked and refuted: the job runs-on ubuntu-22.04, which resolves to GitHub hosted infra, not this repo self-hosted runner (labels self-hosted, Linux, X64, hive-demo, no ubuntu-22.04), confirmed via runner_group_name on the actual failing run.
fix: owui.setup.ts now calls POST /api/v1/users/{id}/update (admin-only, no old-password check) with the current OWUI_E2E_PASSWORD right after the real fixture OAuth login, using that same admin session (GET /api/v1/auths/ for the id). Runs every setup, reconciling Open WebUI local password to the rotated Supabase-side password every night. No assertion weakened or skipped.

title: OWUI nightly Playwright suite 500s on GET /api/v1/users/{id}/profile/image for every fixture user avatar request
error_message: RuntimeError: File at path /data/static/user.png does not exist. (15x per run, the only non-2xx response across 621+ requests once the #712 signin defect was fixed)
root_cause: open_webui.routers.users.get_user_profile_image_by_id falls back to FileResponse(f"{STATIC_DIR}/user.png") whenever profile_image_url is not an http(s) URL or a data: URI. Every OAuth-provisioned account gets exactly that default ("/user.png", set in utils/oauth.py). docker-compose.yml overrides STATIC_DIR to /data/static, bound read-only to deploy/docker/owui-static/ (a repo directory, not the owui-data named volume), and that directory never included a user.png file. Not a volume-persistence bug like #684: a read-only bind sourced from the repo has no first-boot seeding step at all, so the missing file was simply never shipped.
fix: Added deploy/docker/owui-static/user.png, the same badge-mark PNG already reused for logo.png/favicon.png/apple-touch-icon.png/splash.png/splash-dark.png (byte-identical, sha256 confirmed), matching the directory one-asset-every-purpose convention. Documented in the docker-compose.yml volumes comment for that mount.

title: Every chat completion on the demo box was refused because the hive_jwt_forward Open WebUI Function was never installed by any deploy path
error_message: edge-api owui unwrap: "This chat session is not carrying a signed-in user token" (missingUserTokenMessage, apps/edge-api/internal/auth/owui_unwrap.go:127) on every message a member sent from chat-hive.scubed.co; the request body carried no __metadata.upstream_auth
root_cause: hive_jwt_forward is an Open WebUI Function, and Open WebUI has no mount or env var that installs one; only its Functions REST API does, and that requires an authenticated admin session, which cannot exist at container boot. The only caller of that API in the repo was CI's Playwright setup (apps/web-console/e2e/phase-19/owui/owui.setup.ts), so no deployment ever had the filter and per-user attribution had never worked on the box. The absence was silent by construction: no error at boot, no banner, no deploy check, and the deploy went green. The compose comment recorded the manual step and flagged automating it as an open follow-up, which is where it stayed.
