fix: scripts/install-owui-jwt-forward.py is now the single implementation: creates the Filter when absent, refreshes the stored body when it has drifted from the repo source, toggles is_active and is_global only when false (both endpoints flip rather than set, so an unconditional toggle switches the filter off on the second deploy), then re-reads the function from the API and exits nonzero unless it is present, active and global. scripts/owui-mint-admin-token.py obtains the admin session from inside the open-webui container for an admin that already exists, reading WEBUI_SECRET_KEY out of the running server's process environment because backend/start.sh exports it only into the process it execs and a docker exec shell cannot inherit it. deploy-demo-box.yml runs both after the Caddy verification and before the public smoke test. owui.setup.ts now calls the same script with the token of the admin session it just signed in as, so the nightly OWUI suite exercises the deploy's own code.

title: Open WebUI document RAG got 404 from /v1/embeddings because its persisted embedding model was frozen at a pre-catalog value
error_message: 404, message='Not Found', url='http://edge-api:8080/v1/embeddings' (written onto every uploaded file record by Open WebUI)
root_cause: Open WebUI treats every rag.* setting as persistent config: the environment only seeds its own database on first boot, and Config.seed_defaults thereafter inserts nothing that already exists ('Existing DB values take precedence over defaults'). docker-compose.yml carried RAG_EMBEDDING_MODEL=text-embedding-3-small from 2026-05-18 (#143) until 2026-07-26 (#447), when it became the Hive catalog alias, so the demo box kept sending the OpenAI model id. No alias matches it in public.model_aliases, so route selection returned not-found and the gateway answered 404 model_not_found. The 404 body did name the model, but Open WebUI embeds through aiohttp raise_for_status, which discards the body and records only the bare reason phrase, so the failure read as an unregistered route and two investigations chased routing instead of the model name. Ruled out by evidence rather than assumption: allow_all_models is true on both live shim keys, both accounts have a tenant_billing_accounts row, hive-embedding-default has two healthy embedding-capable routes, and the deploy workflow's own sdk-replay job embedded successfully against the box with that alias the same day.
fix: deploy/docker/owui-patches/hive_rag_env_config.py, spliced into open_webui.config.seed_registered_defaults by apply_rag_env_config_patch.py at image build, reconciles exactly four persisted keys (rag.embedding_engine, rag.embedding_model, rag.openai.api_base_url, rag.openai.api_key) from the container environment on every start, and logs the reconciled model without the key value. Per-key rather than ENABLE_PERSISTENT_CONFIG=false, so every other setting an administrator changes in Open WebUI's UI still persists. The model is never hardcoded: it comes from RAG_EMBEDDING_MODEL, which compose derives from OWUI_RAG_EMBEDDING_ALIAS (D-001). Proven on the real image before and after: same persisted stale row and same environment, main sends text-embedding-3-small, patched sends hive-embedding-default.
prevention: Any Open WebUI setting expressed as a compose environment variable is inert on a deployment that has already booted. Reconcile it explicitly or expect the running system to diverge from the repo. CI cannot catch this class: owui-nightly boots a fresh Open WebUI every run, where first-boot seeding always agrees with the environment.

title: The launcher clearance spec failed at 1440px because it located Open WebUI's model selector by an aria-label that only exists while no model is selected
error_message: Error: OWUI model selector at 1440px / expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed / Locator: locator('button[aria-label="Select a model"]') / Error: element(s) not found, at apps/web-console/e2e/phase-19/owui/09-agent-workspace-launcher.spec.ts:114:7 (owui-nightly runs on dfc50f73 and the two before it, both attempts)
root_cause: Open WebUI labels one model-selector button two ways: aria-label 'Select a model' while nothing is selected and 'Selected model: <id>' once something is (i18n keys 'Select a model' and 'Selected model: {{modelName}}'). 09-agent-workspace-launcher.spec.ts waited on the first form before measuring header clearance, so its handle on the selector was only valid while the e2e catalogue came back empty, which is the state the spec's own comment records as normal. Once #735 and #737 made models resolve, Open WebUI auto-selected one, the label changed, and the wait failed on the first width of the loop, before any bounding box was read. The failure read as a 768px overlap defect because of the test name, but no geometry was ever measured and the CSS was never involved. 03-chat-model-switch.spec.ts and 06-tenant-model-visibility.spec.ts had already hit the identical rot at run 28688154897 and switched to a regex matching both forms; spec 09 was written without that fix.
fix: Locate the selector by the id upstream depends on itself: button[id^="model-selector-"][id$="-button"]. The pinned v0.10.2 bundle assigns that id unconditionally alongside aria-expanded, and its own model-selector keyboard shortcut calls document.getElementById("model-selector-0-button").click(), so the id is present in every state the button has and cannot be renamed upstream without breaking upstream. Verified live in both states: id model-selector-0-button with aria-label 'Selected model: hive-auto' when the catalogue serves a model and with 'Select a model' when /api/models is stubbed empty. The text-node walk that widens the selector now skips whitespace-only nodes, which would otherwise leave the header at its original width and get reported as a launcher defect. custom.css's measurement table gained two corrections found while measuring: its right-edge figures are the selector's own and the add-model button adds about 22px past them (520 not 498 at 768px, so 94px of clearance not 116px), and a selected model makes upstream render a 'Set as default' button, which sits on its own line and never enters the launcher's row.
prevention: An aria-label that renders differently per state is not a locator. Before waiting on one, check whether the element also carries an id or role the application itself depends on. A spec whose handle is only valid in one state passes for as long as the environment happens to sit in that state, and the failure then surfaces far from its cause: this one failed at 1440px inside a test named for 768px, and a fix aimed at the test's name would have relaxed a working geometry assertion. Also: a green overlap assertion proves nothing without a forced-overlap control, so the proof capture includes one.

error_message: PUT /api/budget/{id} and POST /api/spend-alerts/{id} returned 404 from the console; a tenant owner could not save a hard spend cap or create a spend alert.
root_cause: budgets.Handler.ServeHTTP dispatched /api/v1/budgets/ and /api/v1/spend-alerts/ since Phase 14, but neither prefix was ever registered on the router, so every request fell through to the /api/v1/ catch-all and 404'd. Not an identifier mismatch: the console already sent viewer.current_account.id and the backend keys on public.accounts.id. The handler was correct and unreachable. The budgets package tests drove the handler directly with httptest.NewRequest, so an unmounted prefix was invisible to them, and the budget page swallowed the read with .catch(() => null) while the e2e spec deferred the save round trip by its own header comment.
fix: Registered both prefixes on the router and added router_budgets_test.go, which asserts dispatch through NewRouter (not against the handler) and fails with the exact reported 404 when the mounts are reverted.

error_message: POST /api/v1/accounts/current/api-keys returned Next.js 404 HTML; API keys could not be created or revoked, and the checkout modal could not load rails or start a checkout.
root_cause: Four Client Components fetch a relative /api/v1/accounts/current/... path. That namespace belongs to the control-plane and has never existed in the console app: no route handler under app/api/v1/, no rewrites in next.config.ts, no middleware proxy. Next served its own 404 page. The typed server client already had correct createApiKey, revokeApiKey, getCheckoutRails and initiateCheckout; nothing browser-side was wired to them. Issue #552 fixed the identical mistake on the per-key limits page one call site at a time, which is how the siblings survived.
fix: Added one console route handler with an explicit allowlist delegating to the typed client, plus browser-api-routes.test.ts, which walks the real files and asserts every relative /api/... a Client Component fetches has a matching route handler. It goes red on exactly the four broken paths.

title: The console ADMIN group was unreachable for the account that owns the workspace, because feature gates and the marketplace were gated on platform admin
error_message: /console/feature-gates and /console/marketplace both rendered the EmptyState "Admin access required" for a tenant OWNER, after is_platform_admin was stripped from the demo accounts
root_cause: Two workspace-scoped surfaces were mounted behind RoleService.RequirePlatformAdmin in platform/http/router.go. Their data is per tenant (tenant_settings rows keyed by the caller selected tenant, marketplace_tenant_entries keyed the same way), so the authority they needed was OWNER of that tenant, not the platform-wide flag that also grants credit minting and provider base_url rewrites. While the demo account carried is_platform_admin the mismatch was invisible; stripping that flag, which was correct, made the organization owner unable to administer the organization.
fix: platform.WorkspaceAdminGate admits the OWNER of the tenant on the session (tenant_users, ACTIVE) or a platform admin, and stamps the platform-admin overlay into the request context. Feature gates and the marketplace mount behind it. Two carve-outs stay platform-only inside the handlers and are advertised on the wire so the console renders no refused control: feature gates in the billing and admin categories (manageable=false), and catalog curation, which writes the one global marketplace_entries table every tenant reads (can_curate=false). Provider CRUD and credit grants were not touched.
prevention: Gate on the scope of the data, not on the biggest flag that happens to be true for the person testing. A per-tenant row wants the tenant role; a global table wants the platform role. Also: viewer.TenantID is the only safe source of scope here, since deriving authority from any owner membership of any flagged account is the cross-workspace leak of issue #750.

title: The workspace admin gate was unit tested, its attachment to the two routes was not, so deleting either mount kept the suite green
error_message: No error. Deleting the gate Require call from the feature-gate mount, and separately from the marketplace mount, left the whole control-plane short suite green
root_cause: Tests covered the predicate and the handler carve-outs; nothing dispatched through NewRouter, so no assertion depended on the middleware still being wired. The mutant lets any MEMBER with a selected tenant administer their own workspace gates. The same gap had been found once for the providers mount and the pattern was not carried to the new mounts.
fix: router_workspace_admin_test.go builds a router with a stub gate that records that it ran and refuses, and asserts all four workspace-scoped admin paths are answered by the gate, not the handler. A second test asserts a nil gate leaves the routes unmounted rather than falling back to a wider gate.
prevention: A middleware test proves the middleware. Only a router dispatch test proves it is installed. Verify by deleting the mount line, not by reading it.

title: ENABLE_ADMIN_PANEL was a dead compose key on Open WebUI v0.10.2
error_message: No runtime error. docker-compose.yml set ENABLE_ADMIN_PANEL=false and two comments reasoned from it as if it were an active control.
root_cause: The name exists nowhere in the pinned ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:v0.10.2 image, verified by grepping the image's own backend rather than only the upstream tag. It arrived with the rest of the service block in #143, exactly as ENABLE_MODEL_FILTER did. Same class: a plausible-looking Open WebUI variable copied from an older release or a third-party hardening guide, never checked against the pinned source. ENABLE_PLUGINS, recommended by those guides for hiding the workspace, is dead in this release too.
fix: Deleted the key and rewrote the two comments in docker-compose.yml and Dockerfile.open-webui that cited it as the reason Open WebUI's model registry stays empty. Every Open WebUI variable introduced by #772 was checked against the pinned image first.

error_message: phase-19 spec 09-agent-workspace-launcher asserted a[href="/notes"] is visible and clicked it, while the same PR removed Notes and 404d the route at Caddy
root_cause: the spec used a sidebar entry as its drawer-opened fixture; the removal PR never ran the owui e2e project, and PR CI does not run it either, so the break would have surfaced only in the nightly
fix: drawer-opened proof moved to a[href="/workspace"], the nav loop dropped /notes, and an explicit toHaveCount(0) on a[href="/notes"] added after the visible Workspace link so the absence is not vacuous. Verified live: old assertion FAILs on the patched stack, new assertion PASSes there and FAILs on a stack with ENABLE_NOTES back on

error_message: a Rewrite.find string in hive_ui_surfaces.py edited so it no longer matches the shipped Open WebUI bundle passed every test in scripts/test_owui_ui_surfaces.py
root_cause: the bundle test built its input out of rewrite.find itself, so it could never notice that find had drifted off the real bundle; the only real guard runs inside the image build, and ci.yml runs make test-scripts without ever building Dockerfile.open-webui
fix: checked in deploy/docker/owui-patches/pinned-bundle-excerpts.json, verbatim slices of the pinned digest bundle produced by dump_bundle_excerpts.py, and assert every find matches those real bytes exactly once plus that the fixture image equals the digest the Dockerfile pins, so a digest bump forces a regeneration instead of going green

error_message: Caddyfile.owui @blocked path_regexp anchored at ^/+ never covered the /api/v1 mount; GET /api/v1/configs/export and GET /openai/config returned the live gateway key and oauth.client_secret to any admin session
root_cause: Every alternative in the regex sat behind the ^/+ anchor, so only bare SPA routes matched. POST /api/v1/auths/signup and the /api/v1/auths/admin/* family were never blocked. Separately the two credential-bearing config reads had no rule at all, and @adminMutation only inspects mutation verbs so a GET was never evaluated.
fix: Added an api(?:/v[0-9]+)? arm covering auths/(signup|admin) and configs/export, plus a top-level openai/config arm. All segment-exact, never prefixes: a configs* prefix would catch /api/v1/configs/banners which the front end reads on every page load, and an openai* prefix would catch /openai/models and /openai/chat/completions. Must-stay-open list captured from a real signed-in session Caddy access log against the pinned image, not from source. Removed dead /api/v*/admin* and /api/v*/roles* globs from @adminMutation (no such OWUI routers). Pinned by scripts/test_caddy_owui_blocklist.py in make test-scripts.

title: Open WebUI shipped an unauthenticated-to-admin terminal proxy and a settings panel that routed tool calls to any URL, and neither had a front-door block
error_message: No runtime error. GET /api/v1/configs/tool_servers and GET /api/v1/configs/terminal_servers answered 200 on the public chat origin with a tenant-owner admin session, and every route on /api/v1/terminals answered on get_verified_user alone, including the any-verb proxy at /{server_id}/{path:path} and the websocket at /{server_id}/api/terminals/{session_id}.
root_cause: Two halves that only look like one problem. Server side, routers/terminals.py in v0.10.2 gates nothing on get_admin_user, so a registered connection is usable by any verified user in its group scope, with the credential the connection was registered with attached server side; that is an authenticated request-forgery primitive against the compose network. Caddyfile.owui never listed /api/v1/terminals at all. Client side, the Settings > Integrations panel registers direct tool servers, which the browser calls at the configured URL itself, so no proxy rule on the origin can see that traffic at all. direct_tool_servers:false does not hide the panel because SettingsModal.svelte shows the tab when role is admin OR the permission is set, and every tenant owner is an Open WebUI admin here (#748). v0.10.2 has no ENABLE_ADMIN_PANEL key, so there is no configuration that removes it.
fix: Caddyfile.owui @blocked gained a terminals arm and configs/(tool_servers|terminal_servers) arms, all segment-exact so /api/v1/configs/banners, /api/v1/configs/models, /api/v1/configs/connections and /api/v1/tools/ stay open. deploy/docker/owui-patches/remove_integrations_tab.py deletes the settings-tab descriptor from the built SPA bundle at image build, which closes the nav button, the settings search keyword route and the showSettings(tools) deep link at once, because all three are driven from that filtered descriptor list. scripts/test_caddy_owui_blocklist.py now also asserts the Dockerfile still runs that patch, so the two halves cannot drift apart in either direction.
prevention: Match the descriptor, not the guard, when patching a minified bundle: the descriptor is built from source string literals and survives minification, the guard is optional chaining over mangled locals that a rebuild renames. And check what the client does with a non-2xx before adding a block: GET /api/v1/terminals/ is issued on every page load, so blocking it looked like an outage until its caller turned out to return an empty list on any non-2xx, which is why the block costs one console line and nothing else.

error_message: scripts/test_caddy_owui_blocklist.py asserted the substring remove_integrations_tab.py appeared somewhere in Dockerfile.open-webui, which the COPY line satisfies on its own
root_cause: the check pinned a filename rather than an invocation, so neutering the RUN line while leaving the COPY in place kept the test green even though the image patch never executed and the Settings > Integrations panel shipped back
fix: parse the Dockerfile into logical instructions across backslash continuations and assert separately that a COPY stages the script and a RUN executes it with python3; both mutations now fail the test

title: Console checkout proxy forwarded credits above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, silently rounded
error_message: checkout initiate with credits 9007199254740993 returned 200 and forwarded 9007199254740992
root_cause: The route checked credits for type, finiteness, integrality and sign but never for magnitude, and JSON numbers are float64 so anything past Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER arrives already rounded. The control-plane had no upper bound either: the per-rail maxima it advertises were never enforced.
fix: Bounded credits by Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER in the console route, matching the sibling budget proxy, and gave ValidatePurchaseAmount the rail so InitiateCheckout enforces the maximum it advertises.

title: Console proxy mapped every upstream refusal to 502 because its error branch was unreachable
error_message: A non-owner creating an API key received 502 Failed to create API key, identical to the control-plane being down
root_cause: The route branched on ControlPlaneError, but createApiKey, revokeApiKey, getCheckoutRails and initiateCheckout all threw a plain Error from readResponseError, so the branch could never be taken and statusSummary was dead code.
fix: Switched those four client functions to throwControlPlaneError, which is what the class exists for and what the sibling proxy routes already rely on.

title: E2E workspace switch helper waited on a URL that never changes, so it never waited at all
error_message: page.reload: net::ERR_ABORTED; maybe frame was detached? (CI) and expect(locator).toHaveCount failed / waiting for navigation to finish (local); console-budgets toBeDisabled received enabled
root_cause: tests/e2e/support/workspace-switch.ts awaited page.waitForURL(url => url.pathname.startsWith("/console")) after selecting a workspace. The account-switch handler always 303s back to /console, so the URL is identical before and after the switch, and playwright-core Frame.waitForURL short-circuits to waitForLoadState whenever the current URL already matches the pattern. The wait resolved immediately without observing the navigation, so the next page.reload or page.goto raced the in-flight POST and the switch was lost. The product was correct throughout: the switch persists across a reload and the destination workspace enforces its owner gate.
fix: Wait for the next page load event, which is per document rather than per URL, and short-circuit when the target workspace is already selected because React does not dispatch onChange for an unchanged select value so no navigation would occur. Raised the two specs to a 120s budget since each drives seven or eight server-rendered navigations.

title: Live integration went red on main because control-plane made exactly one attempt to reach a shared, contended pooler
error_message: dependency failed to start: container hive-control-plane-1 is unhealthy; container log: WARNING: database not available at startup: failed to ping database: FATAL: (EMAXCONNSESSION) max clients reached in session mode - max clients are limited to pool_size: 15
root_cause: The Supabase session-mode pooler is capped at 15 clients shared by CI, agents and the live deployment, and a push to main starts two full-stack CI jobs within one second of each other, each booting a control-plane with pool_max_conns=6. control-plane called platformdb.Open once, about two seconds into a 145 second healthcheck window, and captured DBReady as a static bool, so losing that one race left the process serving a 503 /health for its whole life with 143 seconds of the window unused.
fix: Added db.OpenWithRetry, which retries the open for a 75 second budget that fits inside the compose start_period, and returns immediately on the new db.ErrConfig sentinel so a missing DSN or a transaction-mode pooler still fails fast. control-plane boot now uses it, and the redis probe context is created after the open so a slow open cannot expire it.

title: Session-mode pooler exhausted by idle pgxpool connections
error_message: FATAL: (EMAXCONNSESSION) max clients reached in session mode - max clients are limited to pool_size: 15
root_cause: A Supavisor session slot is held for as long as the pgxpool connection that owns it exists, not for as long as it is used. pgxpool defaults pool_max_conn_idle_time to 30 minutes and pool_health_check_period to 1 minute, so any control-plane that ever burst to pool_max_conns=6 pinned six of the fifteen shared slots for the next half hour while idle. Three mostly-idle consumers (demo box, a developer stack, one CI job) exhausted the ceiling between them. Measured 2026-08-10 with no CI running: six parallel session-mode connections were all refused.
fix: scripts/derive-pooler-dsn.py now adds pool_max_conn_idle_time=60s and pool_health_check_period=15s to the session DSN, and lists both in PGX_ONLY_PARAMS so the libpq flavour still strips them. Guarded by TestSessionPoolReleasesIdleConnections, which counts live server backends before and after the idle window.

error_message: Playwright web-e2e flaked at 7.7 percent: two profile-completion specs passed only on retry
root_cause: The Supabase fixture reseed runs in test.beforeEach, which shares the test timeout, so a reseed measured between 2.6s and 30.2s left the product a random slice of its declared 30s budget. It also ran through execFileSync, freezing the worker event loop so Playwright timeout timer could not fire, and one test was reported passed at 30194ms under a 30000ms timeout.
fix: Shared helper tests/e2e/support/fixture-reset.ts runs the reseed as an awaited async child with its own 120s ceiling and adds its measured wall time back via testInfo.setTimeout, so the product always gets the full declared budget. Applied to all nine specs that copy-pasted the hook.

error_message: Session-authenticated chat served inference with no charge, no usage event and no recorded verdict; 80 traces across 4 tenants in 5 days all recorded zero tokens and zero credits
root_cause: jwtAwareChatHandler routed a populated auth.UserFrom to chat.Handler, which wrote llm_traces and audit_log only: no hold, no settlement, no verdict. The budget middleware could not cover it either, since it resolves workspace identity from an hk_ bearer alone, so a zero-balance workspace still served. rewriteDispatchBody never set stream_options.include_usage, so the terminal usage frame never arrived and the token counts behind any charge were always zero. The branch dated to 2026-05-18; PR #735 moved all Open WebUI traffic onto it by fixing per-user identity injection, which turned a dormant design into live free serving.
fix: chat.Handler now resolves the tenant's billing account and deployment posture in one lookup, refuses an unmapped tenant, an unpriceable alias and an account that cannot pay before any provider call, takes a 10000 credit hold, forces stream_options.include_usage through metering.RewriteBody, and settles exactly once at the served route's catalog price with the real token counts, releasing the hold in full on every failure path. Control-plane carries the metered tokens onto the settlement usage event so console analytics reads real quantities (#856). ENTERPRISE_EDGE tenants stay explicitly non-billable per D-027.

error_message: Pressing Enter in the deployed chat composer sent nothing: no POST /api/chat/completions, no error, prompt left in the composer, while the send arrow worked with the same text
root_cause: Not upstream Open WebUI and not the Hive patch layer. The shared demo account had the per-user preference settings.ui.ctrlEnterToSend set to true (Settings > Interface > Input, Enter Key Behavior). With it on, Enter inserts a newline and only Ctrl+Enter sends, while the send arrow submits the same form either way, which is exactly the reported asymmetry. Nothing in Hive writes that key; an automated sweep over the settings surface of the shared account left it set and nothing checked it afterwards. Both the stock open-webui v0.10.2 image and the Hive patched image sent on Enter when run locally, which ruled out the image before anything was changed.
fix: Reset the account's preference to false, and added apps/web-console/scripts/demo-chat-settings.mjs, which mints an audited live session, reads the account's Open WebUI settings, exits 1 on drift from the demo-safe values, and repairs them with --repair. Wired into the DEMO.md pre-demo verification list. Proof of the before and after states is in docs/proof/issue-855-enter-key.

error_message: agent task Blocked: engine: start conversation: Post http://agent-server.control/api/conversations: EOF
root_cause: controlclient.WaitReady treated a dialable Unix socket as readiness. The socat shim inside the SIF creates that socket in the first line of the image runscript, while the Python agent-server behind it needs tens of seconds to bind, so the first request after the wait hit a shim whose TCP target was not listening and got a bare EOF.
fix: WaitReady now requires a real HTTP response from /health before returning, and the default ControlReadyTimeout went from 30s to 3 minutes to cover a measured cold start. Separately, CreateTask ran the launch on the caller request context, so a closed browser tab cancelled a live launch; the launch and its transitions now run on context.WithoutCancel with their own timeout.

title: Open WebUI knowledge retrieval always timed out at 60s on the demo box
error_message: POST /api/v1/retrieval/query/collection returned 504 Gateway time-out after 60s for a single-chunk collection, so no knowledge-backed chat answer was ever possible
root_cause: ENABLE_RAG_HYBRID_SEARCH was persisted true while no reranking model is configured. Open WebUI builds a RerankCompressor for every hybrid query and, with reranking_function None, re-embeds the query and every retrieved document to score them (backend/open_webui/retrieval/utils.py), so one question costs three gateway embedding round trips. Each takes 7 to 17 seconds through the gateway, which exceeds Caddyfile.owui response_header_timeout of 60s. The flag also lives in Open WebUI persisted config, so the compose value only ever seeded on first boot and no later compose edit could move it.
fix: Default ENABLE_RAG_HYBRID_SEARCH to false in docker-compose.yml behind OWUI_RAG_HYBRID_SEARCH, and reconcile rag.enable_hybrid_search from the environment on every boot in owui-patches/hive_rag_env_config.py. Retrieval then returns 200 in about 32s and a knowledge-backed chat answer arrives in about 29s with its citation.

title: A form blocked by HTML5 required validation looks like a dead button to a DOM coverage gate
error_message: workspace:knowledge/create::button::Create Knowledge -> no effect (mutations=0)
root_cause: Both fields carry the HTML5 required attribute and the form sets no novalidate, so the browser refuses the submit before any handler runs. The browser paints its validation bubble outside the DOM, so a MutationObserver based gate records zero mutations and zero requests and reports the control as silent when a person actually sees Please fill out this field.
fix: No code change. Verified live with form.checkValidity() false and validationMessage populated, and captured the bubble in a screenshot. A DOM coverage gate that flags a control as doing nothing must first check checkValidity on the enclosing form before it can call the control dead.

error_message: Hive chat surface shipped the retired forest-green mark (#0d3b2e on #f8f7f4) and 404d on /static/favicon-dark.png, web-app-manifest-192x192.png, web-app-manifest-512x512.png and site.webmanifest
root_cause: Two independent causes. First, the owui-static assets were drawn from the superseded hive.scubed.co brand; the current brand lives in a separate repo (scubedcombd/scubed) behind https://scubed.co/hive, so a sweep that checked this repo found nothing wrong. Second, an asset that is ABSENT cannot be found by auditing the assets that are present: every file in owui-static was on-brand while the files the browser actually requested (favicon-dark.png on every dark /auth load, the PWA manifest icons) did not exist at all. Size mismatches had the same shape: manifest.json declared logo.png as 500x500 while the file was 256x256, which is grounds for a browser to reject the icon and substitute its own.
fix: Regenerated every raster from deploy/docker/owui-static/generate-brand-assets.py using the palette in scubedcombd/scubed src/app/(frontend)/styles.css and the hexagon from hive-hero.tsx. Added the four missing files, rendered each asset at the size its consumer declares, updated the two inline copies of the mark in loader.js and custom.css, and patched the Open WebUI manifest description in Dockerfile.open-webui. Verified by walking a running container with a real browser window: zero 4xx, favicon-dark.png now resolves.

title: LiteLLM wiring lint attributed the credential to a sibling field, not the recipient
error_message: apps/edge-api/internal/metering: is handed the LiteLLM address or master key in apps/edge-api/cmd/server/main.go but never calls SelectRoute
root_cause: tools/lint-litellm-dispatch-requires-routing.mjs walked back from resolveLiteLLMBaseURL() to the nearest preceding package-qualified identifier on any line. Adding Billing: &metering.PGBillingAccountResolver{Pool: dbPool} above LiteLLMURL: inside the same chat.Deps literal moved attribution onto metering, which only ever receives a database pool. Worse than a false positive: it is a false negative on the package actually handed the credential, so the wiring rule can be pointed away from any real recipient by inserting one package-qualified sibling field.
fix: Attribute to the type of the composite literal or call that lexically encloses the resolver, located with a brace and paren counter walking outward through nested literals. Self-test covers the sibling-field, nested-literal and positional-argument shapes alongside the original rogue case. Verified by injecting a rogue recipient into main.go and confirming the lint still exits non-zero.

error_message: cannot load module /app/packages/dbtest listed in go.work file: open /app/packages/dbtest/go.mod: no such file or directory
root_cause: Go Dockerfiles stage go.work member manifests layer by layer and packages/dbtest was added to go.work without adding its COPY pair, so every image bake died at go mod download
fix: added the same manifest+source COPY pair packages/embedmodel already gets to all five Go Dockerfiles and added packages/dbtest/* to the ci.yml web_e2e path allowlist (PR #1159)

error_message: TestAccountingConcurrentGetBalanceDuringReserve race: WARNING: DATA RACE read of l.barrier unsynchronized with write l.barrier=nil
root_cause: deterministic test barrier stored nil under mutex but readers dereferenced it unlocked after the peer agent's 27ca9a1bc rewrite; equality fires at most once so the nil write is unnecessary
fix: dropped the nil assignment in GetBalance, kept the bounded-wait equality barrier (PR #1159 commit 1ce8b197e)

error_message: 150 deepseek-v4-pro calls, 30.2M credits burned by CI in one day on uat-test-hive-s-workspace
root_cause: HIVE_TOOLS_MODEL defaulted to deepseek-v4-pro in ci.yml, deploy-demo-box sdk-replay env, docker-compose sdk-tests default and the js suite fallback because free-pool aliases lack tools capability; owner's free-tier instruction was implemented for the chat lane only
fix: repointed all four sites to deepseek-v4-flash (tools_supported=true, healthy) and added a ci.yml declare-billing guard that exits 1 if the resolved tools model is deepseek-v4-pro (PR #1200)

error_message: cache read/write tokens written as zero into api_key_usage_rollups while usage_events carried real counts
root_cause: finalize HTTP request structs and FinalizeReservationInput had no cache token fields, so the rollup write received literal zeros; sync and stream paths additionally never sent input/output tokens
fix: plumbed CacheReadTokens/CacheWriteTokens through edge finalize call, both services' input structs, the rollup write and the completed usage_event literal, with red-then-green tests at both surfaces (PR #1204)

error_message: 403 account_not_provisioned on every /v1/* call for a freshly minted API key with no operator-visible signal anywhere but the HTTP response
root_cause: AuthSnapshot.TenantUUID (apps/edge-api/internal/authz/authz.go) returned ErrAccountNotProvisioned silently; qa-tester@hive.test specifically was a non-owner MEMBER of an old shared E2E fixture tenant (created 2026-04-25, before the tenant_billing_accounts table existed) whose billing mapping was already claimed by a different member's account, and both live provisioning entry points (signup.Provisioner.Reconcile, accounts.Service.EnsureViewerContext) short-circuit on any existing ACTIVE tenant_users row so neither could ever revisit it
fix: added a log.Printf at TenantUUID's single choke point so every occurrence is operator-visible; live-repaired qa-tester by setting its stale tenant_users row to SUSPENDED and re-running the existing self-serve tenant-provision endpoint, which mapped its own account cleanly; verified with a freshly minted key against api-hive.scubed.co (200, real catalog); the check itself was extracted in review as exported authz.ParseTenantID(TenantLookup), which TenantUUID now delegates to and which the images and audio routing adapters (two further silent call sites found in the same review) also call, and the log line records account_id plus the offending tenant_id and deliberately omits key_id (CodeQL clear-text-logging alert #31)
verified_new_signups_unaffected: traced signup.Provisioner.Reconcile + accounts.Service.provisionDefaultWorkspace on current main (c177972f4) and confirmed via the live control-plane boot log that both provisioning entry points are wired and running; no commit merged 2026-08-28 touched internal/signup, internal/accounts, or their main.go wiring

error_message: Direct inference streaming path (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions) never forced stream_options.include_usage upstream, so a caller that did not set it itself got no terminal usage frame from a provider requiring it and settlement captured the full reservation hold instead of the exact charge
root_cause: metering.RewriteBody was wired into the chat-orchestrator path (internal/chat/dispatch.go) but never into internal/inference's executeStreaming, which dispatched the caller's original body untouched aside from a model-name rewrite in litellm_client.go's dispatch()
fix: Force metering.RewriteBody before dispatch in executeStreaming, gated per provider via new metering.SupportsIncludeUsage (groq, openrouter allowlist). Strip the resulting usage-bearing frame from the client-visible stream when the caller's own request did not set include_usage, so billing consumes it internally without changing the public contract.

error_message: local batch executor's output.jsonl carried a raw upstream response body verbatim into a customer-retrievable file
root_cause: apps/control-plane/internal/batchstore/executor/dispatcher.go's Dispatch success branch wrote InferencePort's ChatCompletion response body directly into OutputResponse.Body with no sanitization, unlike every sync/stream boundary edge-api normalizes (PR #1222)
fix: extracted PR #1222's id-mint + frame-sanitize logic into shared module packages/sanitize (edge-api's mint_id.go/upstream_cost.go now delegate to it); dispatcher.go calls sanitize.VariablePriceFrame before constructing each line's OutputLine

error_message: anon and authenticated held ALL privileges on all 82 public-schema tables on the demo box, and anon could EXECUTE the SECURITY DEFINER function public.agent_tasks_list_active()
root_cause: an early revision of 20260828_01_service_role_public_schema_grant.sql granted ALL on all tables, sequences and functions in public to anon, authenticated and service_role plus matching ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES, and rag-demo-readiness.yml applied it to the live box before review; narrowing the file afterwards did not withdraw the grants already made, and REVOKE FROM PUBLIC is no defence against a direct grant to a named role
fix: migration now revokes tables, sequences, functions and the matching default privileges from all three API roles before re granting only service_role plus the five documented authenticated tenant-table grants, made idempotent and self-healing; ci-throwaway-db.sh asserts anon holds nothing, authenticated holds nothing outside those five tables, and anon cannot execute agent_tasks_list_active, with a negative control (PR #1257)

error_message: rag-demo-readiness reported 'chunk relayed after finish_reason' against a branch that fixes exactly that leak
root_cause: the job pointed EDGE_API_URL at the stack's own edge-api container, which serves the last deployed build, so it verified main and never the checkout under review
fix: the job now starts a second edge-api on the same compose network with the checkout bind-mounted, runtime config copied from the live container, and verifies against that one; live stack untouched (PR #1257)

error_message: go build inside the PR edge-api container failed with 'error obtaining VCS status: exit status 128', then after that fix the container exited 126 with 'Permission denied' running the freshly built binary
root_cause: the runner workspace is a git repo owned by the runner user while the container runs as root, so git refuses it and Go's default VCS stamping fails; separately, docker mounts a tmpfs noexec by default and that tmpfs is where air writes the binary it then executes
fix: GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false, and the tmpfs mount now requests exec explicitly; the wait loop also fails fast on 'failed to build' instead of burning the full timeout (PR #1257)

error_message: verify-rag-roundtrip.py reported '3 hits but no marker' on all three attempts against a healthy RAG pipeline
root_cause: the script never deleted the documents it ingested, so nineteen near-identical fixture notes had accumulated in its throwaway tenant and crowded the newest marker out of a top_k=3 search; the check degraded the more often it ran
fix: purge_stale_fixtures deletes its own prefixed leftovers older than any live run before ingesting, and the run's own document is deleted in a finally block so a failed run does not poison the next one; parse_created_at unit tested (PR #1257)

error_message: POST /v1/files answered a blind 500 with the storage error discarded, making every file and batch failure undiagnosable
root_cause: apps/edge-api/internal/files/handler.go wrote the customer-facing 500 and dropped err on the floor, so nothing in the compose logs said why an upload failed. The underlying cause it was hiding: the CI S3_ENDPOINT secret still points at the Supabase Cloud project this repo left in August, and that hostname no longer resolves
fix: log the error at the point of failure with bucket, size and content type, customer-facing message unchanged. Endpoint secret tracked as issue #1324

error_message: usage.prompt_tokens_details was present in one live run and absent in the next on the same alias
root_cause: normalizeReasoningUsage existed for exactly this and had no caller anywhere in the tree, so the gateway relayed whatever the upstream sent instead of guaranteeing the OpenAI shape
fix: called from normalizeChatCompletion before the response is marshalled, with a unit test that fails if the call goes missing again

error_message: live-integration metered 70048 tokens against a 6000 ceiling
root_cause: the oversized-body probe in typed-exceptions.test.ts sent about 300KB of prompt, and nothing on the chat path rejects a body that size, so all of it was forwarded upstream and metered as prompt tokens. max_tokens bounded only the output
fix: probe reduced to a tenth of the size, ceiling raised to 20000 with the measurement and the suite growth from 22 to roughly 50 completions written down beside it

error_message: multi-turn tool round trip intermittently returns an empty assistant message on the second turn, after the tool result goes back
root_cause: deepseek-v4-flash spends most of its ceiling on hidden reasoning (measured live: 22 to 182 reasoning tokens out of 49 to 231 completion tokens at ceiling 256), and when reasoning overruns the ceiling the upstream answers content null with finish_reason length. The existing zero-content retry guard was gated on route.reasoning_reserve_tokens greater than zero, a column that enumerates three free-pool routes and nothing else, so it never ran for this route
fix: gate the guard on the response shape (empty length completion) rather than the catalogue column, in apps/edge-api/internal/inference/orchestrator.go. The inverted regression test carries the measurement

error_message: both max_tokens conformance assertions were incapable of failing
root_cause: they asserted usage.completion_tokens against the caller ceiling, and clampUsageToCeiling rewrites that exact field to the caller ceiling on every fixed-price alias so the customer reads what they are billed. Both aliases under test are fixed price, so the assertion measured the clamp rather than the ceiling
fix: both tests now also bound the visible content length, which the clamp does not touch

error_message: analytics-billing-page-wiring.test.tsx timed out under full-suite load after adding prior-period/cache-sample/top-keys fetches to the overview tab
root_cause: five independent control-plane fetches were awaited sequentially on every overview page load instead of concurrently, adding real latency in production and pushing one test's wall time past the 5000ms default timeout under parallel CI load
fix: restructured the analytics overview data-fetching, extracted in review to apps/web-console/lib/analytics/overview-fetch.ts, into five async helper functions (fetchMain, fetchPreviousUsage, fetchCacheSample, fetchPreviousCacheSample, fetchTopKeys), each swallowing its own errors, and run them all through one Promise.all instead of five sequential awaits

error_message: analytics overview tiles showed figures the account never measured: an unsampled sparkline bucket drawn as a 0 percent cache hit rate, and a measured zero prior period rendered as No prior data
root_cause: Sparkline coalesced a null bucket to 0, and derivePeriodDelta merged fetch failure, absent prior figure and measured zero into one branch
fix: nulls reach Recharts intact with connectNulls off, derivePeriodDelta takes the failure flag as its own argument and returns fromZero for a real move off a measured zero, blended price passes its null through, plus a component test and three page level tests (PR #1276)

error_message: no runtime error: the console privacy page as first written rendered a blanket no-content-stored claim that is false for /v1/batches, /v1/files and /v1/rag, plus a product-wide provider-blindness claim disproved by catalogue summaries that name vendors (#1284), a metering claim anchored to the console-side UsageEventRow projection rather than the usage_events table, and a 1:1 alias-to-route claim that is a property of seed data rather than of SelectRoute
root_cause: the console privacy page published four content-storage claims the system does not enforce: a blanket no-content-stored statement that was false for /v1/batches, /v1/files and /v1/rag, a structural claim resting on UsageEventRow (a console-side projection that omits internal_metadata, customer_tags and provider_request_id from the real usage_events table), a product-wide provider-blindness claim disproved by catalogue summaries that name vendors (#1284), and a 1:1 alias-to-route claim that is a property of seed data rather than of SelectRoute, which returns FallbackRouteIDs with no same-provider constraint
fix: rescoped every claim to what the code enforces, named the three surfaces that do store content with their deletion routes, disclosed the litellm data_collection posture and the upstream-error-text logging exception, added a what-this-page-does-not-cover card, split catalog fetch failure from an empty catalog, and anchored the metering claim with a Go guard over every INSERT INTO public.usage_events column list plus negative page assertions that fail if any corrected sentence returns

error_message: deploy-drift-watchdog.yml's grace-window freshness check read main's tip commit date instead of the newest covered commit's date, so an unrelated uncovered commit landing shortly after a genuinely stale covered commit reset the apparent freshness and masked real deploy drift
root_cause: the freshness step used gh api on steps.resolve.outputs.head_sha (main's tip) rather than determining which commit in the base..head range actually touched a path deploy-demo-box.yml's paths filter covers
fix: added .github/ci/newest-covered-commit.mjs (reuses pushPaths/isCovered from lint-deploy-paths-filter.mjs) to find the newest covered commit in range; the workflow step now reads that commit's date via local git log instead of head_sha via gh api

error_message: scripts/set-compose-project-name.sh --check silently passed on a real compose-project-name collision when the colliding working directory's path happened to contain this worktree's compose_dir as a substring
root_cause: the collision filter used grep -v -F (fixed-string substring match) instead of grep -vxF (whole-line match) to remove this worktree's own compose_dir from the docker-reported collision list, so any line merely containing compose_dir as a substring was wrongly treated as a self-match and dropped
fix: changed grep -v -F to grep -vxF on line 81 of scripts/set-compose-project-name.sh so only an exact line match is removed

error_message: a demoted workspace owner keeps platform.WorkspaceAdminGate authority indefinitely after a Members-page demotion
root_cause: public.tenant_users.role was written once at signup/reconciliation and never updated again; accounts.Service.UpdateMemberRole only ever wrote public.account_memberships.role, so the two role stores could diverge permanently and never converge
fix: accounts.Service.UpdateMemberRole now propagates its role change onto tenant_users via the new signup.SyncTenantMembershipRole (resolved through public.tenant_billing_accounts); a backfill migration reconciles existing demotion drift; a second migration grants hive_app read access to tenant_billing_accounts

error_message: the issue #1245 propagation fix could itself write tenant_users.role = OWNER onto a personal tenant's row, granting WorkspaceAdminGate and egress authority the personal-tenant MEMBER hardcode exists to withhold
root_cause: the sync assumed UpdateMemberRole can never fire for a personal tenant because a single-member account rejects role changes, but Service.CreateInvitation has no account_type guard and 20260727_02 widened account_invitations.role to include owner, so a personal account can hold a second owner who then promotes the original user; the same CASE also flattened the four-value tenant_users role domain onto two values and could promote a non-ACTIVE row
fix: gate the promotion arm of SyncTenantMembershipRole on tenants.personal_owner_user_id IS NULL and tenant_users.status = ACTIVE, preserve any non-OWNER tenant role with ELSE tu.role, leave the demotion arm unconditional, run the sync on context.WithoutCancel, and drop the same-role early return so a re-issued role repairs a failed propagation

title: API key credit-limit cadence select had no observable effect and was unprovable by the interaction gate
error_message: /console/api-keys select|#key-reset-cadence -> unproven: activation produced no request, no navigation, and no change to the rendered output (enabled by filling key-nickname, key-expires, key-credit-limit)
root_cause: The select was disabled until the credit limit field was non-empty. The interaction gate's disabled branch satisfies the precondition and then re-activates the control with a click, and a click never changes a select's value, so the control was unreachable by the only means the gate has of exercising a select. Independently, changing the cadence altered React state and nothing rendered, so a customer setting a per-month cap got no acknowledgement that the amount they were typing meant per month rather than lifetime.
fix: Removed the disabled gating and made the cadence drive rendered text: the credit limit field's hint restates what the amount means under the chosen cadence, and a summary line states the bound edge-api will enforce. Pinned by three tests in api-key-create-form.test.tsx.

title: Console reported a credit limit for API keys that were not capped
error_message: no runtime error; the keys list rendered a dollar ceiling beside a key whose budget_kind was none
root_cause: UpdatePolicy upserts budget_limit_credits with COALESCE, so a nil means leave unchanged rather than clear, and a key moved to budget_kind none keeps the ceiling it last carried. Enforcement ignores it (edge-api authz.CheckAccess requires a non-none kind AND a non-nil limit) but the keys list decided capped-or-not from the limit alone, so removing a cap left the old figure on screen next to a key that could spend the whole account balance. Reachable from the browser through the api-keys policy proxy route, which accepts budget_kind none.
fix: buildKeyView reports no limit when the kind enforces nothing, fixing every consumer of the view at once. Pinned by TestKeyViewHidesALimitThatIsNotEnforced, asserted against buildKeyView directly because the in-package stub repository overwrites the column instead of COALESCEing it and a stub-driven test could not go red.

title: A network failure applying an API key credit cap discarded the key's one-time secret
error_message: Failed to create key. Please try again.
root_cause: The cap is applied in a second request after the key already exists, and that request sat inside the same try block as key creation. A transport failure threw into the outer catch, which sets the generic create-failed error and never renders the secret panel, so the customer was told nothing had been created while holding a real, live, uncapped key whose only copy of the secret had just been discarded.
fix: The policy call has its own try block; a refusal and a transport failure both produce the same warning, which now says the key is live and uncapped, and the secret panel still renders. Pinned by a test that rejects the second fetch and asserts the secret is still shown.

title: Latency column tests named guards they never asserted, and nothing crossed the wire seam
error_message: Test named "renders a formatted latency column and an em-dash for an unmeasured request" asserted only getByText("1.8s"); mutating the cell to formatLatencyMs(row.latency_ms ?? 0) left the suite 32/32 green. Separately, no test carried latency_ms across the JSON boundary: deleting the client decoder line left the suite 17/17 green and http_test.go asserted nothing about the key.
root_cause: Two coverage shapes that cannot fail. The em-dash case had a fixture row but no assertion on it, and the three other columns that also render an em-dash would have made a naive text query pass anyway. The wire seam had a wiring test whose fixture omitted the new field entirely, so the only test running the real decoder never exercised the line under test.
fix: Resolve the Latency cell by its header position and assert both the formatted value and the em-dash. Put latency_ms on the wiring test's mocked response body and assert the rendered cell. Add TestListEventsLatencyCrossesTheWire asserting the JSON key is emitted when measured and omitted when not. Verify each by mutation rather than by reading.

error_message: demo walkthrough harness: every wait-up-to-N-ms visibility check timed out identically regardless of timeout value (8s vs 40s made no difference), including chat sign-in itself
root_cause: Playwright locator.isVisible({timeout}) does not poll: the timeout option is deprecated and ignored per playwright-core type declarations, so it is one immediate check that returns false whenever called before the element exists
fix: added a waitVisible(locator, timeoutMs) helper using locator.waitFor({state:"visible", timeout}) and replaced all isVisible({timeout}) call sites in apps/web-console/tests/e2e/demo-walkthrough.mjs

error_message: CodeQL js/incomplete-sanitization (high) on demo-walkthrough.mjs report writer: escaping only the pipe character left the backslash unescaped
root_cause: the markdown table cell escaper ran .replace(/\|/g, "\\|") so an input already containing a backslash produced a literal backslash followed by a live cell separator, and a newline in an error message ended the table row outright
fix: extracted mdTableCell into apps/web-console/tests/e2e/support/md-table.mjs, escaping backslash and pipe in one pass, flattening line separators, and dropping an orphan backslash left by truncation; applied to every cell, with unit tests in tests/unit/md-table-cell.test.ts

error_message: latent credential leak: the walkthrough screenshotted the console right after minting an API key, and the console renders a newly created key in full exactly once, so the committed PNG would have carried a live key into a public repository
root_cause: the capture happened with no masking pass, and the proof linter reads text files only, so nothing in CI, GitHub secret scanning or GitGuardian can inspect a credential burned into pixels; it never fired only because every create call in the evidence set failed
fix: added maskLiveApiKeys (apps/web-console/tests/e2e/support/mask-api-keys.mjs, jsdom tested) sweeping every text node before the shutter and again after it with a retake on a late paint, registered the minted key as a run secret, filled the form's own expiry field, and taught tools/lint-no-token-in-proof-captures.mjs to catch a bare hk_ key

title: Anthropic surface broke the real SDK four ways: content_block_start dropped text, empty completions serialized content null, count_tokens 401d API keys, /v1/models rejected x-api-key and answered OpenAI-shaped
error_message: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'NoneType' and 'str' in anthropic/lib/streaming/_messages.py accumulate_event; TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable on msg.content; anthropic.AuthenticationError 401 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"authentication_error","message":"missing user"}} on count_tokens; anthropic.AuthenticationError 401 invalid_api_key on models.list()
root_cause: Two families. (1) Go zero-value JSON encoding dropped values the Anthropic wire contract requires to be explicitly present: omitempty on StreamContentBlock.Text dropped the required "text":"" from every text content_block_start, and a nil []ResponseBlock in FromOAIResponse marshaled to null instead of []. Neither is visible to a Go-side assertion, since len() cannot distinguish nil from empty and a "" field looks correct until encoding/json runs. (2) The Anthropic surface's auth model only ever covered POST /v1/messages: count_tokens is the only route that does not delegate to the chat chain so it never gained an API-key authority and recognised session principals only, and GET /v1/models never got the leaf APIKeyNormalizer /v1/messages carries, which matters because the global one in authSelectorMiddleware only exists when jwtMW is non-nil.
fix: StreamContentBlock.Text became *string and gained Input json.RawMessage set to {} on tool_use starts, matching the live streaming spec. FromOAIResponse seeds Content with an empty non-nil slice at construction so both exits are covered. anthropic.Deps.AuthorizeAPIKey added and count_tokens accepts either principal, fail-closed when nil, refusals reshaped from the shared WriteAuthFailure mapping. GET /v1/models registered through modelsHandler applying APIKeyNormalizer at the leaf plus a ModelsCompat wrapper that answers Anthropic-shaped callers with the Anthropic list and error envelopes while leaving OpenAI callers byte-identical.
discovered_by: PR #1278's Anthropic Messages conformance suite, which caught the content_block_start case live against the real SDK and shipped it marked xfail against issue #1274; that PR's own buglog entry is folded in here rather than duplicated

title: GET /v1/models leaked upstream provider identity in hive-stt and hive-tts descriptions
error_message: models.list() returned description "Serverless speech-to-text (Groq Whisper) for /v1/audio/transcriptions." and "Serverless text-to-speech (Groq PlayAI) for /v1/audio/speech." live against api-hive.scubed.co
root_cause: public.model_aliases.summary was seeded with the provider name by 20260717_02_voice_groq_stt_tts.sql and is published verbatim as the description field of GET /v1/models and as summary on both catalogue endpoints. Every provider-blindness guard in the repo sat on an error path, so catalogue metadata was never examined. The hive-tts text was additionally stale: Groq deprecated playai-tts on 2025-12-31 and the route has pointed at canopylabs/orpheus-v1-english since that same migration.
fix: Boundary guard in both modules: redactAlias in control-plane's buildCatalogSnapshot and buildPublicCatalogModels, redactSnapshot in edge-api's catalog client fetchSnapshot, scrubbing display name, summary, owned_by and capability badges. Vocabulary is serving-provider identity only, not model vendors, so shipped names such as Deepseek V4 Pro survive. Migration 20260828_01 repairs the two seeded rows behind a still-leaking predicate and raises a NOTICE for any other customer-facing row that names a provider.

title: edge-api buffers request bodies before validating the credential on five routes with no backpressure
error_message: no error surfaced: an unauthenticated caller sending Authorization: Bearer hk_x reaches io.ReadAll on /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/embeddings and /v1/messages, at a measured 20.8 to 30.4 MiB live heap per request, with no rate limit, no concurrency limiter, no ingress proxy, no mem_limit and no GOMEMLIMIT in front of it
root_cause: auth.Selector routes on the hk_ prefix alone and validates nothing, budgetGate passes through on a failed resolve, and Authorize (which carries the rate limiter) runs inside executeSync/executeStreaming, after the handler has already read and buffered the body. The alias needed by Authorize is only known after the body is parsed, which is why the check ended up downstream of the read.
fix: Mitigated, not fixed, in PR #1301: a 60s read deadline armed around each pre-auth body read via internal/httpx.ReadBody and cleared only on a successful read (clearing it on the error path leaves net/http's post-handler body drain unbounded), one shared reader for the inference, anthropic and chat surfaces, http.MaxBytesReader handed the unwrapped *response so its close-after-reply half is not inert behind middleware, mem_limit 1536m plus a non-overridable GOMEMLIMIT 1280MiB with a boot-time cgroup comparison, files.ParseMultipartForm's maxMemory cut from 512 MiB to 32 MiB so one upload cannot pin half the container's memory limit, and Unwrap methods on statusRecorder and responseRecorder so http.ResponseController can reach the connection at all. The ordering fix, validating the credential before the read, is tracked in issue #1299.

title: Upstream error prose reached customers on the RAG chat relay and through the pre-stream sanitizer's forward-by-default tail
error_message: You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details
root_cause: Three defects. (1) /v1/rag/chat's streamGroundedChat sanitized by hand, rewriting model and id and deleting system_fingerprint while forwarding every other key of a parseable frame, so a top-level error object delivered inside a committed 200 reached the customer whole, provider brand and top-up URL included. (2) sanitizeProviderBlindMessage forwarded any upstream message no rule recognized, which is a deny list exactly as wide as its literals: DeepSeek's 402 'Insufficient Balance', 'monthly spend limit', 'past due ... payment information', 'Free tier limit reached' and 'run out of prepaid funds' all passed through verbatim, as did the reported quota sentence on any status other than 429. (3) packages/sanitize keyed its error check on the KEY being present, so an upstream that declares error on every chunk and leaves it null had every content frame refused: silent truncation on both SSE relays and needless retry-to-exhaustion in the batch executor. The session-chat relay did NOT leak an error frame: it already dropped one, which truncated the answer silently instead.
fix: Routed the RAG relay through the shared packages/sanitize allowlist instead of its hand-rolled deny list. Inverted the tail of sanitizeProviderBlindMessage to forward an upstream message only when it is customer-actionable on a request-shaped 4xx status, and deleted the money-vocabulary deny list that had been added first. Keyed the frame error check on the VALUE, treating null, empty string, {}, [] and false as absent. Added sanitize.ReplaceErrorFrame as a separate opt-in call so both SSE relays render a gateway-owned error frame instead of truncating, while VariablePriceFrame's ok==false contract stays intact for the batch dispatcher, which would otherwise store and bill a synthetic error line.

title: max_tokens silently inflated by the reasoning reserve, billing 206x the caller's ceiling; n>1 silently truncated to one choice
error_message: max_tokens: 8 on hive-free returned usage.completion_tokens 1650, all billed; n: 2 returned HTTP 200 with choices.length 1 and no error
root_cause: applyReasoningHeadroom (PR #1225, issue #1171) inflated every completion-limit field the caller had set by provider_routes.reasoning_reserve_tokens (4096 on three of four hive-free members) before dispatch, so max_tokens 8 went upstream as 4104. Its premise that hidden reasoning would burn the reserve while visible content stayed inside the caller's budget is unenforceable: nothing upstream separates the two, so the model spent the inflated ceiling on visible output. Because the rewrite skipped a ceiling the caller had NOT set, its entire effect was overriding ceilings callers HAD set. Separately, ChatCompletionRequest.N and CompletionRequest.N were declared and read by nothing, so n was forwarded, ignored upstream, and one choice returned with no error. Two hold-capture branches (sync zero-content, streaming missing-usage) also charged the flat DefaultHoldText authorization floor regardless of the caller's ceiling, a far larger breach of the same invariant.
fix: Deleted applyReasoningHeadroom and its three call sites so the caller's ceiling reaches the provider unchanged. Added completion_ceiling.go: requestedCompletionCeiling reads the ceiling from the caller's original body before any outbound rewrite, clampUsageToCeiling caps usage.CompletionTokens at it on the single usage object both the response and the charge derive from, rewriteNormalizedUsage keeps the response body in step, and capCaptureAtCeiling bounds both hold-capture branches without ever reaching zero. Refused n other than 1 with 400 unsupported_parameter and param n on both chat and legacy completions.

title: Completion-ceiling fix shipped a caller-triggerable revenue bypass, an unbounded content estimate, and a usage clamp on aliases it could not bill
error_message: Request {max_tokens: 1, max_completion_tokens: 100000} was dispatched unchanged and settled at output_tokens 1, actual_credits 24 where the unclamped generation was worth 6620; a synchronous 200 carrying content and no usage block against max_tokens 8 charged 1323 credits versus 32 ceiling-priced; on an upstream_actual alias the caller read completion_tokens 8 while paying the upstream cost of 1650
root_cause: Three separate causes in one change. First, requestedCompletionCeiling takes the smaller of the two chat spellings but nothing rewrote the outbound body, so after applyReasoningHeadroom was deleted both fields were forwarded verbatim and the request boundary enforced a different number than settlement; OpenAI and Groq both prefer max_completion_tokens, so the larger field governed generation while the smaller governed billing. Second, clampUsageToCeiling returns early when usage is nil, which is the same condition that routes settlement into the content-length estimate in settlementCredits, leaving the one path that guesses the completion count as the one path with no ceiling on it; the streaming path was masked because settleStream overwrites the estimate with a bounded hold capture. Third, clampUsageToCeiling was called unconditionally, but an upstream_actual alias settles from respBody or acc.RawUsageChunk, which the clamp never reads, so it lowered the number the caller reads without lowering the charge.
fix: Added pinCompletionCeiling, which writes the settled minimum back over every ceiling field present in the outbound body before dispatch and only ever narrows, wired on executeSync, executeStreaming and executeResponsesStreaming ahead of EnforceVariablePriceBounds. Added a ceiling parameter to settlementCredits that bounds the content-length completion estimate, with ChatSettlementCredits reading the ceiling from the request bytes it already parses so the session chat surface is covered too. Gated clampUsageToCeiling on route.Pricing.IsUpstreamActual, the same test capCaptureAtCeiling applies. Refused best_of other than 1 on legacy completions. Qualified the support-matrix sentence for the variable-price case and documented that non-positive and non-integer ceiling spellings read as no ceiling.

title: Ceiling pinning kept unreadable fields, the variable-price bound invented a larger ceiling than the caller set, and hold captures priced the prompt at zero
error_message: Request {max_tokens: 1, max_completion_tokens: 100000.5} was dispatched with the float intact; a variable-price request sending only {max_tokens: 1} was dispatched with max_completion_tokens 16384 written in beside it; a streaming request with a prompt of roughly 11334 tokens and max_tokens 8 whose upstream sent no usage block settled at 32 credits rather than the price of the prompt
root_cause: Three causes in the fix for the first adversarial stream. First, pinCompletionCeiling skipped any present ceiling field that failed to unmarshal into int64, on a never-widen rule that does not hold for a value the gateway cannot read at all, since the provider may parse what encoding/json refuses and OpenAI treats max_completion_tokens as authoritative. Second, clampCompletionLimit sets every field the endpoint speaks to VariablePriceMaxCompletionTokens when absent, with no reference to a smaller ceiling already present, and an upstream_actual alias has no settlement clamp behind that. Third, capCaptureAtCeiling computes its bound as the catalog price of the whole request at the ceiling, but both callers pass the metered input count, which is zero exactly because those branches are reached when no usable usage block arrived, so the prompt was priced at nothing and the capture collapsed to the output side alone.
fix: pinCompletionCeiling now keeps a field only when it reads as a positive integer at or below the ceiling and overwrites everything else present, logging the raw literal truncated. clampCompletionLimit derives an effective limit as the lower of VariablePriceMaxCompletionTokens and any smaller positive ceiling already in the body, and uses it both to fill absent fields and to narrow present ones. Added captureInputTokens, which falls back to the content-length prompt estimate settlementCredits already uses when the upstream reported no usage, and wired it into both capCaptureAtCeiling call sites. Added a byte-scan early-out to pinCompletionCeiling so an ordinary single-ceiling chat request pays no extra decode.

title: decision-citation-check hook exited 0 on every Claude Code MultiEdit
error_message: No output, exit 0, on a MultiEdit payload citing a fabricated D-999; the settings matcher invoked the hook and it declined to look
root_cause: The payload reader handled only Cursor's flat data.edits array. Claude Code nests a MultiEdit's edits under tool_input.edits, so ti.content, ti.new_string and the flat editsContent were all empty, content resolved to empty string, and the guard exited before auditing a single citation. The self-check could not see it because its claude payload shape was only ever tool_name Write with tool_input.content, so the MultiEdit shape was never exercised. Same defect as issue #1333 in secrets-scanner.js, inherited by copying the pattern.
fix: Adopt the payload handling that fixed #1333 in secrets-scanner.js: read the edits array from either harness position, serialize any field that is not a string instead of coercing it, and audit every source rather than letting the first truthy one win. Run the decision-citation self-check cases over all three write shapes via the shared edit() helper, plus explicit payloads for content-and-edits together, a non-string new_string, and a fabrication in a later edit. Mutation tested: reverting the edits-array read turns nine cases red.

error_message: The console minted an API key (201, secret shown in the copy-it-now panel, key listed active) for an account with zero public.tenant_billing_accounts rows, and edge-api then rejected that key with 403 account_not_provisioned and an unactionable contact-support message
root_cause: apikeys.Service.CreateKey and RotateKey generated and persisted a secret without ever resolving the account's billing tenant, even though the exact lookup (Repository.GetTenantIDByAccountID) already existed in the same package for ResolveSnapshot; the unprovisioned state is permanent for any user whose tenant is already billed by a different workspace, since tenant_billing_accounts is UNIQUE on both columns and signup.EnsureTenantBillingAccount refuses to guess a mapping
fix: added Service.requireBillingTenant as a precondition on both mints, returning a new ErrAccountNotProvisioned sentinel mapped to 409 with an actionable message and the machine code account_not_provisioned; the console proxy route now maps that code to its own customer-facing wording (it never forwards upstream error text) and ApiKeyCreateForm renders a 409 body verbatim instead of replacing it with generic retry text; ResolveSnapshot deliberately still tolerates uuid.Nil so pre-existing keys keep failing closed at the boundary
verification: four new Go tests plus a mutation check that forces the guard false and confirms all four go red; two new console unit tests; visual proof captured against a branch-built control-plane and console over a throwaway Supabase with all 112 migrations, showing the refusal, zero api_keys rows written, and a positive control where a mapped workspace still issues a key

title: Secrets scanner hook was blind to every MultiEdit and reported clean
error_message: No output, exit 0, on a MultiEdit payload containing a hardcoded credential. Indistinguishable from a clean scan.
root_cause: secrets-scanner.js resolved its edit array from the top-level data.edits field, which is Cursor's file-edit payload shape. Claude Code nests the array at tool_input.edits. On a MultiEdit all three content fallbacks (ti.content, ti.new_string, top-level data.edits) were empty, so content became the empty string and the early-return guard exited 0 with no output. The hooks.selfcheck.js harness fed both harness shapes but used Write for the Claude Code case, whose text lives in tool_input.content, so the nested-array path was never exercised; the harness was also not invoked by CI or any npm script, so even a covering case would not have run.
fix: Consult both shapes, preferring tool_input.edits over data.edits. Add a claude-multiedit shape to hooks.selfcheck.js and run every secrets-scanner case under all three shapes. Wire hooks.selfcheck.js into the Repo policy lints required CI check so the harness actually runs.

title: Playwright spec manifest entry landed outside the specs object
error_message: scripts/verify-spec-collection.mjs would report UNDECLARED tests/e2e/sso-silent-consent.spec.ts runs but is not in the manifest
root_cause: The manifest was rewritten with a JSON serializer that reformatted every array and appended the new spec as a key of the root object rather than of specs, and the guard reads document.specs only. The branch was never re-run against the guard after that edit because the pull request was already conflicting, and a conflicting pull request builds no refs/pull/N/merge, so GitHub created no pull_request run and the page showed only CodeQL, GitGuardian and CodeRabbit, which reads green at a glance.
fix: Resolve the rebase conflict onto main's compact formatting and add the single line inside specs, then run npm run e2e:verify-collection to confirm 42 files collect into the pinned projects.

title: OAuth consent landing redirect guard missed repeated slashes
error_message: ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS between /oauth/consent and itself for an auto-approve target spelled //oauth/consent
root_cause: isSafeRedirectTarget compared parsed.pathname with trailing slashes stripped and nothing else, so //oauth/consent and /oauth//consent matched neither the landing path nor its stripped form and were allowed. Next.js then 308-normalized the repeated slashes away and re-entered the landing, which asked GoTrue again and received the same redirect_url. The guard's comment reasoned about Next normalizing a trailing slash into the guarded path and stopped there, which is why it read as thorough and still missed the sibling case.
fix: Collapse repeated slashes and decode percent escapes inside a try before comparing, and add a unit case that fails against the previous guard. Measured the real routing behaviour against a production console build rather than assuming it: encoded and case variants answer 404, repeated and trailing slashes answer 308.

error_message: n/a
root_cause: console had no privacy/data-policy surface at all (parity re-score, criterion weight 9, credit 0.25)
fix: added /console/privacy grounded in verified backend state (UsageEventRow schema, routing.SelectionInput.AllowedProviders dead code path, provider-blind error handling), never rendering a claim or control that is not enforced; corrected mid-review to drop literal OpenRouter/Groq vendor names per the console-wide provider-blind convention, keeping the third-party-routing disclosure itself

error_message: Anthropic Messages request carrying top_k fails with 400 and the customer-facing message hive-free is not available.
root_cause: edge-api forwards four non-OpenAI fields verbatim from the Anthropic surface (top_k, thinking, cache_control, session_id) because the OpenAI chat-completions shape has no equivalent. hive-free load balances across providers with different tolerances, so the request succeeded or hard-failed depending on which pool member answered, and the refusal reached the caller as model unavailability rather than as a refused field
fix: dispatchWithRetry in apps/edge-api/internal/inference/retry.go now classifies a 400 that names one of those four fields, strips that single field, and retries. Bounded to one strip per field and to attempts that have a successor; a field the caller actually sent is never stripped. Known edge filed as issue #1323

title: Pre-merge frontend gate compiled lib/hive only, so a Hive component added under lib/components was compiled and rendered by nothing
error_message: make test-owui-frontend reported 16 files, 208 tests, 13/13 components compiled, exit 0 on a tree carrying a Svelte parse error, two transposed money figures and an inert settings tab
root_cause: scripts/test-owui-hive-frontend.sh copies upstream components into its scratch tree as text fixtures and runs the svelte compile pass over lib/hive only, so a Hive authored component placed under lib/components/chat/Settings was read as text and never compiled, and no test rendered it; the image build that would have caught the parse error runs after merge in deploy-demo-box.yml
fix: moved the component to vendor/open-webui/src/lib/hive/SettingsUsage.svelte where the compile guard already looks, taught the gate to install the lockfile pinned vite svelte plugin and write a vitest config so tests can import and server side render components, and re-ran the three mutations to confirm each one turns the suite red

title: /v1/messages reported usage input_tokens 0 and output_tokens 0 while billing charged correctly
error_message: usage: {input_tokens: 0, output_tokens: 0} on every POST /v1/messages response
root_cause: The post-finish chunk suppression in apps/edge-api/internal/inference/mint_id.go recognised a terminal usage frame as usage != nil AND len(choices) == 0. LiteLLM v1.98.0 sends that frame with one empty-delta choice, so the relay dropped the only usage frame on the stream.
